translations.literal: The Northern Qi Imperial Clan: Various Princes, Part One
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi Imperial Clan: Various Princes, Part One

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十九齊宗室諸王上

translations.literal: Biography 39: The Northern Qi Imperial Clan—Various Princes, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Biography 39: The Northern Qi Imperial Clan—Various Princes, Part One

sentences.zh: 趙郡王琛子睿清河王嶽子勱廣平公盛陽州公永樂襄樂王顯國上洛王思宗子元海弟思好平秦王歸彥兄子普長樂王靈山神武諸子

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen, his son Rui; Prince of Qinghe Yue, his son Mo; Duke of Guangping Sheng; Duke of Yangzhou Yongle; Prince of Xiangyue Xian'guo; Prince of Shangluo Sizong, his son Yuanhai, and younger brother Sihao; Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, his nephew Pu; Prince of Changle Lingshan; and the sons of Emperor Shenwu
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen and his son Rui; Prince of Qinghe Yue and his son Mo; Duke of Guangping Sheng; Duke of Yangzhou Yongle; Prince of Xiangyue Xian'guo; Prince of Shangluo Sizong and his son Yuanhai, with his younger brother Sihao; Prince of Pingqin Guiyan and his nephew Pu; Prince of Changle Lingshan; and the sons of Emperor Shenwu

sentences.zh: 趙郡王琛，字元寶，齊神武皇帝之弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen, styled Yuanbao, was a younger brother of Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen, whose style name was Yuanbao, was the younger brother of Gao Huan, posthumously honored as Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 少便弓馬，有志氣。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled with bow and horse and possessed resolute ambition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was adept with bow and horse and possessed a resolute spirit.

sentences.zh: 封南趙郡公，累遷定州刺史、六州大都督，甚有聲譽。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Southern Zhao Commandery, and through successive promotions became Governor of Ding Province and Grand Commander of Six Provinces, winning great renown.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Southern Zhao Commandery, rose through successive appointments to Governor of Ding Province and Grand Commander of the Six Provinces, and earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 及斛斯椿等釁結，神武帥師入洛陽，以晉陽根本，召琛留總相府政事，天平中，除御史中尉。

translations.literal: When Husun Chun and others formed a treacherous alliance, Shenwu led his army into Luoyang; because Jinyang was the foundation of his power, he summoned Chen to remain behind and oversee the affairs of the Chancellor's office. In the Tianping era he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Husun Chun and others entered a treacherous compact, Gao Huan led his forces into Luoyang. Because Jinyang was the base of his power, he recalled Chen to remain in charge of the chancellor's office affairs. During the Tianping era Chen was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 正色糾彈，無所回避，遠近肅然。

translations.literal: He impeached with stern countenance and shrank from nothing; near and far were awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated wrongdoing with stern impartiality and shrank from nothing; people near and far were awed into discipline.

sentences.zh: 尋亂神武后庭，因杖而斃。

translations.literal: Before long he violated Shenwu's inner quarters and was beaten to death for it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he violated Gao Huan's inner quarters and was beaten to death for it.

sentences.zh: 時年二十三。

translations.literal: He was twenty-three at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-three years old at the time.

sentences.zh: ，太尉、尚書令，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: [He was posthumously made] Grand Commandant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 天平三年，又贈假黃鉞、左丞相、太師、錄尚書事，進爵為王，配享神武廟廷。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianping he was further granted the ceremonial yellow axe, Left Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat; his rank was advanced to prince, and he was granted a place in the sacrifices at Shenwu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianping he was further granted the ceremonial yellow axe, the posts of Left Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat; his rank was advanced to prince; and he was granted a place in the sacrifices at Gao Huan's temple.

sentences.zh: 子睿嗣。

translations.literal: His son Rui succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui succeeded to his title.

sentences.zh: 睿小名須拔，幼孤，聰慧夙成，特為神武所愛，養于山公主也。

translations.literal: Rui's childhood name was Xubamo. Orphaned young, he was intelligent from childhood and especially beloved by Shenwu, who had him raised by the Princess of Mount Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's childhood name was Xubamo. Orphaned while young, he showed precocious intelligence and was especially beloved by Gao Huan, who had him raised by the Princess of Mount Shan.

sentences.zh: 令游娘母之，恩異諸子。

translations.literal: He had Youniang serve as his foster mother, and the favor shown him differed from that shown to the other sons.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had Youniang act as his foster mother, and the affection shown him differed from that shown to the other sons.

sentences.zh: 魏興和中，襲爵南趙郡公。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era of Wei he succeeded to the title of Duke of Southern Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xinghe era of Wei he succeeded to the title of Duke of Southern Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 年至四歲，未嘗識母。

translations.literal: By the age of four he had never met his mother.
translations.idiomatic: By the age of four he had never met his mother.

sentences.zh: 其母魏華陽山主也。

translations.literal: His mother was the Princess of Mount Hua in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was the Princess of Mount Hua of Wei.

sentences.zh: 其從母姊鄭氏戲謂曰：「汝是我姨兒，何倒親遊氏？

translations.literal: His elder cousin on his mother's side, Lady Zheng, teased him, saying, "You are my nephew by the maternal line—why do you favor the You clan instead?"
translations.idiomatic: His elder cousin on his mother's side, Lady Zheng, teased him, saying, "You are my nephew by the maternal line—why do you cleave to the You family instead?"

sentences.zh: 」睿因訪問，遂失精神。

translations.literal: Rui thereupon made inquiries, and his spirits fell into distress.
translations.idiomatic: Rui thereupon made inquiries, and his spirits sank into distress.

sentences.zh: 神武疑其感疾，睿曰：「兒無患苦，但聞有所生，欲得暫見。

translations.literal: Shenwu suspected he had fallen ill. Rui said, "Your son has no illness; I only heard that I have a birth mother and wish to see her briefly."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan suspected he had fallen ill. Rui said, "Your son has no affliction; I only heard that I have a birth mother and wish to see her briefly."

sentences.zh: 」神武驚，命元夫人至，就宮見之。

translations.literal: Shenwu was startled and ordered Lady Yuan to come so that Rui might see her at the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was startled and ordered Lady Yuan to come so that Rui might see her at the palace.

sentences.zh: 睿前跪拜，因抱頸大哭。

translations.literal: Rui advanced, knelt and bowed, then embraced her neck and wept loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Rui advanced, knelt and bowed, then embraced her neck and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 神武甚悲傷，謂平秦王曰：「此兒至孝，吾子無及者。

translations.literal: Shenwu was deeply grieved and said to the Prince of Pingqin, "This boy is supremely filial; none of my sons can match him."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was deeply moved and said to the Prince of Pingqin, "This boy is supremely filial; none of my sons can match him."

sentences.zh: 」遂為休務一日。

translations.literal: He thereupon suspended official business for a day.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon suspended official business for a day.

sentences.zh: 睿讀《孝經》，至「資于事父」，輒流涕噓欷。

translations.literal: When Rui read the Classic of Filial Piety and came to the phrase "take support in serving one's father," he would weep and sob.
translations.idiomatic: When Rui read the Classic of Filial Piety and came to the phrase "take support in serving one's father," he would weep and sob aloud.

sentences.zh: 十歲喪母，神武親送至領軍府。

translations.literal: At ten he lost his mother; Shenwu personally escorted the coffin to the headquarters of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he lost his mother; Gao Huan personally escorted the coffin to the headquarters of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 為發哀，舉聲殞絕，三日水漿不入口。

translations.literal: When mourning was proclaimed, he cried out until he collapsed; for three days he took neither water nor gruel.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was proclaimed, he cried out until he collapsed; for three days he took neither water nor gruel.

sentences.zh: 神武與武明太后殷勤敦譬，方漸順旨。

translations.literal: Shenwu and Empress Dowager Wuming earnestly exhorted and comforted him, and only then did he gradually comply.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan and Empress Dowager Wuming earnestly exhorted and comforted him, and only then did he gradually comply with their wishes.

sentences.zh: 居喪長齋，骨立，杖而後起。

translations.literal: During mourning he observed long fasting until he was skin and bone, and could rise only leaning on a staff.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he observed long fasting until he was skin and bone, and could rise only by leaning on a staff.

sentences.zh: 神武令常山王與同臥起，日夜喻之，並敕左右，不許進水。

translations.literal: Shenwu had the Prince of Changshan sleep and rise with him, admonishing him day and night, and also ordered those about him not to let water be brought in.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had the Prince of Changshan sleep and rise with him, admonishing him day and night, and also ordered those about him not to let water be brought in.

sentences.zh: 雖絕清漱，午輒不肯食，由是神武食必呼與同案。

translations.literal: Although he ceased rinsing his mouth, at noon he still refused food; because of this Shenwu, whenever he ate, would summon Rui to share his table.
translations.idiomatic: Although he ceased even rinsing his mouth, at noon he still refused food; because of this Gao Huan, whenever he ate, would summon Rui to share his table.

sentences.zh: 神武崩，哭泣嘔血。

translations.literal: When Shenwu died, Rui wept until he vomited blood.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan died, Rui wept until he vomited blood.

sentences.zh: 及壯，將婚，貌有戚容。

translations.literal: When he reached manhood and was about to marry, his countenance still bore grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached manhood and was about to marry, his countenance still bore grief.

sentences.zh: 文襄謂曰：「我為爾娶鄭述祖女，何嫌而不樂？

translations.literal: Wenxiang said to him, "I have taken Zheng Shuzu's daughter for you in marriage—why are you displeased and not glad?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang said to him, "I have taken Zheng Shuzu's daughter for you in marriage—why are you displeased and not glad?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「自痛孤遺，方從婚冠，彌用感切。

translations.literal: He replied, "Having long grieved my orphaned state, I am only now entering the capping and marriage years; this makes me feel all the more keenly."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Having long grieved my orphaned state, I am only now entering the capping and marriage years; this makes me feel all the more keenly."

sentences.zh: 」言未卒，鳴咽不自勝，文襄為之憫然。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking he sobbed uncontrollably; Wenxiang was moved to pity for him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished speaking he sobbed uncontrollably; Wenxiang was moved to pity for him.

sentences.zh: 勱之勤學，常夜久方罷。

translations.literal: Rui was diligent in study and often did not stop until late at night.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was diligent in his studies and often did not stop until late at night.

sentences.zh: 文宣受禪，進爵為王。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan received the abdication, Rui's rank was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan received the abdication, Rui's rank was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 睿身長七尺，容儀其偉，閑習吏事，有知人之鑒。

translations.literal: Rui stood seven feet in height, with imposing bearing; he was versed in administrative affairs and had a discerning eye for men.
translations.idiomatic: Rui stood seven feet in height, with imposing bearing; he was versed in administrative affairs and had a discerning eye for men.

sentences.zh: 天保二年，出為定州刺史、六州大都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao he went out as Governor of Ding Province and Grand Commander of Six Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianbao he went out as Governor of Ding Province and Grand Commander of the Six Provinces.

sentences.zh: 時年十七，稱為良牧。

translations.literal: He was seventeen at the time and was called an excellent governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventeen at the time and was acclaimed as an excellent governor.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔睿領兵監築長城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year an edict ordered Rui to lead troops in supervising the building of the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict ordered Rui to lead troops in supervising the construction of the Long Wall.

sentences.zh: 于時六月，睿途中屏蓋扇，親與軍人同勞苦。

translations.literal: It was then the sixth month; on the road Rui set aside canopy and fan and personally shared hardship with the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: It was then the sixth month; on the road Rui set aside canopy and fan and personally shared hardship with the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 定州先常藏冰，長史宋欽道以睿冒熱，遣倍道送冰，正遇炎盛，咸謂一時之要。

translations.literal: Ding Province had long stored ice; the Chief Administrator Song Qindao, seeing Rui suffer the heat, sent ice by forced marches. It happened to be the height of summer, and all said it was a timely need.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Province had long stored ice; the Chief Administrator Song Qindao, seeing Rui suffer the heat, sent ice by forced marches. It happened to be the height of summer, and all said it was a timely necessity.

sentences.zh: 睿對之歎曰：「三軍皆飲溫水，吾何義獨進寒冰！

translations.literal: Rui sighed at this and said, "The whole army drinks warm water—what justice is there in my alone taking ice!"
translations.idiomatic: Rui sighed at this and said, "The whole army drinks warm water—what justice is there in my alone taking ice!"

sentences.zh: 」遂至銷液，竟不一嘗，兵人感悅。

translations.literal: The ice melted away to liquid, and in the end he did not taste it once; the soldiers were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The ice melted away to liquid, and in the end he did not taste it once; the soldiers were moved and pleased.

sentences.zh: 先是役罷，任其自歸，丁壯先返，羸弱多致僵殞。

translations.literal: Previously, when corvée labor ended, men were allowed to return on their own; the strong went back first, and many of the weak collapsed and died on the way.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when corvée labor ended, men were allowed to return on their own; the strong went back first, and many of the weak collapsed and died on the way.

sentences.zh: 睿於是親帥營伍，強弱相持，賴全者十三四焉。

translations.literal: Rui thereupon personally led the camps so that strong and weak supported one another; those who survived thanks to this were only thirteen or fourteen in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Rui thereupon personally led the camps so that strong and weak supported one another; only thirteen or fourteen in ten survived thanks to this.

sentences.zh: 八年，除都督、北朔州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Beishuo Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Beishuo Province.

sentences.zh: 睿撫慰新遷，量置烽戍，備有條法，大為兵人所安。

translations.literal: Rui comforted the newly resettled population, measured out beacon posts and garrisons, and had complete regulations; the soldiers were greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Rui comforted the newly resettled population, measured out beacon posts and garrisons, and established complete regulations; the soldiers were greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 無水處禱而掘井，泉源湧出，至今號曰趙郡王泉。

translations.literal: Where there was no water he prayed and dug a well; a spring gushed forth, and to this day it is called the Well of the Prince of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Where there was no water he prayed and dug a well; a spring gushed forth, and to this day it is called the Well of the Prince of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 九年，濟南以太子監國，因立大都督府，與尚書省分理眾事，仍開府置佐史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, because the Prince of Jinan was crown prince and supervised the state, a Grand Commander's office was established to divide affairs with the Imperial Secretariat, and a princely establishment with aides and clerks was opened.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, because the Prince of Jinan as crown prince supervised the state, a Grand Commander's office was established to divide affairs with the Imperial Secretariat, and a princely establishment with aides and clerks was opened.

sentences.zh: 文宣特崇其選，除睿侍中，攝大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Wenxuan especially honored the selection and appointed Rui Palace Attendant and acting Chief Administrator of the Grand Commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan especially honored the selection and appointed Rui Palace Attendant and acting Chief Administrator of the Grand Commander's office.

sentences.zh: 睿後因侍宴，帝從容謂常山王演等曰：「由來亦有如此長史不？」

translations.literal: Later, when Rui attended a banquet, the emperor said at ease to the Prince of Changshan Yan and others, "Has there ever been such a chief administrator as this?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Rui attended a banquet, the emperor said at ease to the Prince of Changshan Yan and others, "Has there ever been such a chief administrator as this?"

sentences.zh: 皇建初，兼併州事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he also held the affairs of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian he also held the affairs of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 孝昭帝臨崩，預受顧托，奉迎武成於鄴，拜尚書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao was near death he received the dying entrustment, welcomed Wucheng at Ye, and was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao was near death he received the dying entrustment, welcomed Wucheng at Ye, and was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天統中，追贈父琛假黃鉞；

translations.literal: In the Tiantong era his father Chen was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow axe;
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiantong era his father Chen was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow axe;

sentences.zh: 母元氏贈趙郡王妃，諡曰貞昭，華陽長公主如故。

translations.literal: his mother, the Yuan clan, was posthumously made Princess of Zhao Commandery with the posthumous title Zhenzhao, while her title as Princess of Changhua remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: his mother of the Yuan clan was posthumously made Princess of Zhao Commandery with the posthumous title Zhenzhao, while her title as Princess of Changhua remained as before.

sentences.zh: 有司備禮儀，就墓拜授。

translations.literal: The relevant offices prepared the ritual, and the titles were conferred at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices prepared the ritual, and the titles were conferred at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 時隆冬盛寒，睿跣步號哭，面皆破裂，嘔血數升。

translations.literal: It was then deep winter and bitter cold; Rui walked barefoot, wailing as he went, until his face split open and he vomited several sheng of blood.
translations.idiomatic: It was deep winter and bitter cold; Rui walked barefoot, wailing as he went, until his face split open and he vomited several sheng of blood.

sentences.zh: 及還，不堪參謝。

translations.literal: When he returned he could not bear to attend court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he could not bear to attend court audiences.

sentences.zh: 帝親就第看問，拜司空、攝錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The emperor personally visited his residence to inquire after him and appointed him Minister of Works and acting Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally visited his residence to inquire after him and appointed him Minister of Works and acting Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 河清三年，周師及突厥至并州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Heqing, Zhou troops and the Turks reached Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing, Zhou troops and the Turks reached Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 武成戎服，將以宮人避之，睿叩馬諫，乃止。

translations.literal: Wucheng put on military dress and was about to flee with the palace women; Rui seized his horse's bridle and remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng put on military dress and was about to flee with the palace women; Rui seized his horse's bridle and remonstrated, and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝親禦戎，六軍進止，並令取睿節度，而使段孝先總焉。

translations.literal: The emperor personally took command; advance and halt of the six armies were all ordered to follow Rui's direction, while Duan Xiaoxian was placed in overall command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally took command; advance and halt of the six armies were all ordered to follow Rui's direction, while Duan Xiaoxian was placed in overall command.

sentences.zh: 帝與宮為被緋甲，登故北城以望，軍營甚整。

translations.literal: The emperor and the palace women donned crimson armor and climbed the old north wall to look out; the army camps were very orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and the palace women donned crimson armor and climbed the old north wall to look out; the army camps were very orderly.

sentences.zh: 突厥咎周人曰：「爾言齊亂，故來伐之。

translations.literal: The Turks reproached the men of Zhou, saying, "You said Qi was in disorder, and so we came to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks reproached the men of Zhou, saying, "You said Qi was in disorder, and so we came to attack it.

sentences.zh: 今齊人眼中亦有鐵，何可當邪！

translations.literal: Now the men of Qi have iron even in their eyes—how can they be withstood!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the men of Qi have iron even in their eyes—how can they be withstood!"

sentences.zh: 」乃還。

translations.literal: They then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 至陘嶺，凍滑，乃鋪氈以度。

translations.literal: At Yin Ridge the ground was frozen and slippery, so they spread felt to cross.
translations.idiomatic: At Yin Ridge the ground was frozen and slippery, so they spread felt to cross.

sentences.zh: 胡馬寒瘦，膝已下皆無毛，比至長城，死且盡。

translations.literal: The barbarian horses were chilled and thin; below the knee they had no hair, and by the time they reached the Long Wall nearly all were dead.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian horses were chilled and thin; below the knee they had no hair, and by the time they reached the Long Wall nearly all were dead.

sentences.zh: 乃截槊杖之以歸。

translations.literal: They then cut spear-shafts to use as walking sticks on the return.
translations.idiomatic: They then cut spear-shafts to use as walking sticks on the return.

sentences.zh: 是役也，段孝先持重，不與賊戰，自晉陽失道，為虜所屠，無遺類焉。

translations.literal: In this campaign Duan Xiaoxian was cautious and did not engage the enemy; he lost the road from Jinyang and was slaughtered by the invaders, none escaping.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign Duan Xiaoxian was cautious and did not engage the enemy; he lost the road from Jinyang and was slaughtered by the invaders, none escaping.

sentences.zh: 斛律光自三堆還，帝以遭大寇，抱其頭哭。

translations.literal: Hulü Guang returned from Sandui; because of the great calamity the emperor embraced his head and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Guang returned from Sandui; because of the great calamity the emperor embraced his head and wept.

sentences.zh: 任城王湝進曰：「何至此！

translations.literal: The Prince of Rencheng Tang advanced and said, "Why go so far!"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Rencheng Tang advanced and said, "Why go so far!"

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He then stopped.

sentences.zh: 光面折孝先於帝前，曰：「段婆善為送女客。

translations.literal: Guang openly rebuked Xiaoxian before the emperor, saying, "Old woman Duan is good at escorting women guests."
translations.idiomatic: Guang openly rebuked Xiaoxian before the emperor, saying, "Old woman Duan is good at escorting women guests."

sentences.zh: 」於是以睿為能，加尚書令，封宣城郡公，拜太尉，監五禮。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon regarded Rui as capable, added the post of Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xuancheng Commandery, appointed him Grand Commandant, and put him in charge of the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon regarded Rui as capable, added the post of Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xuancheng Commandery, appointed him Grand Commandant, and put him in charge of the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 晚節頗以酒色為和士開所構。

translations.literal: In his later years he was largely framed by He Shikai on account of wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was largely framed by He Shikai on account of wine and women.

sentences.zh: 睿久典朝政，譽望日隆，漸被疏忌。

translations.literal: Rui had long directed court government; his fame and standing grew daily, and he was gradually viewed with suspicion and jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Rui had long directed court government; his fame and standing grew daily, and he was gradually viewed with suspicion and jealousy.

sentences.zh: 乃撰古忠臣義士，號曰《要言》，以致其意。

translations.literal: He thereupon compiled ancient loyal ministers and righteous men, calling the work Essential Words, to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon compiled ancient loyal ministers and righteous men, calling the work Essential Words, to express his intent.

sentences.zh: 武成崩。

translations.literal: Wucheng died.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng died.

sentences.zh: 葬後數日，睿與馮翊王潤、安德王延宗及元文遙奏後主云：「和士開不宜仍居內。

translations.literal: Several days after the burial, Rui, together with the Prince of Fengyi Run, the Prince of Ande Yanzong, and Yuan Wenyao, memorialized the Later Lord, saying, "He Shikai should not remain within the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Several days after the burial, Rui, together with the Prince of Fengyi Run, the Prince of Ande Yanzong, and Yuan Wenyao, memorialized the Later Lord, saying, "He Shikai should not remain within the palace."

sentences.zh: 」併入奏太后。

translations.literal: They also entered together to memorialize the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: They also entered together to memorialize the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 因出士開為袞州刺史。

translations.literal: He Shikai was therefore sent out as Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai was therefore sent out as Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 太后欲留過百日，睿正色不許。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wished to keep him for a hundred days more, but Rui sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wished to keep him for a hundred days more, but Rui sternly refused.

sentences.zh: 太后令酌酒賜睿，睿正色曰：「今論國家大事，非為厄酒。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered wine poured and bestowed on Rui; Rui said with stern countenance, "We are now discussing great affairs of state, not drinking because of ill fortune."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered wine poured and bestowed on Rui; Rui said with stern countenance, "We are now discussing great affairs of state, not drinking because of ill fortune."

sentences.zh: 」言訖便出。

translations.literal: When he had spoken he went out at once.
translations.idiomatic: When he had spoken he went out at once.

sentences.zh: 其夜，睿方寢，見一人長可丈五尺，臂丈餘，當門向床，以臂壓睿，良久遂失。

translations.literal: That night, as Rui was about to sleep, he saw a man about one zhang five chi tall with arms more than one zhang long standing at the door facing his bed, pressing on Rui with his arms; after a long while he vanished.
translations.idiomatic: That night, as Rui was about to sleep, he saw a man about one zhang five chi tall with arms more than one zhang long standing at the door facing his bed, pressing on Rui with his arms; after a long while he vanished.

sentences.zh: 甚惡之，起坐歎曰：「大丈夫運命一朝至此！

translations.literal: Greatly alarmed, he rose and sighed, saying, "A great man's fate has in a single morning come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Greatly alarmed, he rose and sighed, saying, "A great man's fate has in a single morning come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」旦欲入朝，妻子咸諫止之。

translations.literal: At dawn he wished to enter court; his wife and children all admonished him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he wished to enter court; his wife and children all admonished him to stop.

sentences.zh: 睿曰：「社稷事重，吾當以死效之。

translations.literal: Rui said, "The affairs of altars and state are weighty; I ought to offer my life in service.
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, "The affairs of altars and state are weighty; I ought to offer my life in service.

sentences.zh: 吾寧死事先皇，不忍見朝廷顛沛。

translations.literal: I would rather die serving the late emperor than bear to see the court overturned."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die serving the late emperor than bear to see the court overturned."

sentences.zh: 」至殿門，又有人曰：「願勿入。

translations.literal: At the palace gate another man said, "I beg you not to enter."
translations.idiomatic: At the palace gate another man said, "I beg you not to enter."

sentences.zh: 」睿曰：「吾上不負天，死亦無恨。

translations.literal: Rui said, "I am not false to Heaven above; even in death I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, "I am not false to Heaven above; even in death I have no regret."

sentences.zh: 」入見太后，太后復以為言，睿執之彌固。

translations.literal: He entered and saw the Empress Dowager; she again spoke on the matter, but Rui held all the more firmly to his position.
translations.idiomatic: He entered and saw the Empress Dowager; she again spoke on the matter, but Rui held all the more firmly to his position.

sentences.zh: 出至永巷，被送華林園，於雀離佛院令劉桃枝拉殺之，時年三十六。

translations.literal: When he went out to the Eternal Lane he was sent to Hualin Park, where at the Sparrow-departure Buddha Hall Liu Taozhi was ordered to strangle him; he was thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out to the Eternal Lane he was sent to Hualin Park, where at the Sparrow-departure Buddha Hall Liu Taozhi was ordered to strangle him; he was thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 大霧三日，朝野冤惜之。

translations.literal: Heavy fog lasted three days; court and country mourned him as wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy fog lasted three days; court and country mourned him as wronged.

sentences.zh: 其年，詔聽以王禮葬，竟無贈諡。

translations.literal: That year an edict permitted burial with princely rites, but in the end no posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict permitted burial with princely rites, but in the end no posthumous title was granted.

sentences.zh: 子整信嗣，好學有行檢，位儀同三司，後終於長安。

translations.literal: His son Zhengxin succeeded him; he loved learning and had proper conduct, rose to the third rank of Yitong, and later died in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengxin succeeded him. He loved learning and conducted himself with integrity, rose to the third rank of Yitong, and later died in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 清河王岳，學洪略，神武從父弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Qinghe Yue, styled Honglue, was a younger cousin of Shenwu on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qinghe Yue, whose style name was Honglue, was Gao Huan's younger cousin on the father's side.

sentences.zh: 父翻，字飛雀，以器度知名，卒於侍御中散。

translations.literal: His father Fan, styled Feique, was known for magnanimity and died as Attendant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan, whose style name was Feique, was known for magnanimity and died while serving as Attendant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 元象中，贈假黃鉞、大將軍、太傅、太尉、錄尚書事，諡孝宣公。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow axe, Grand General, Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous title Duke Xiaoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow axe, the posts of Grand General, Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous title Duke Xiaoxuan.

sentences.zh: 嶽幼孤貧，人未之知。

translations.literal: Yue was orphaned young and poor; people did not yet know him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was orphaned while young and poor; people did not yet know him.

sentences.zh: 長而敦直，姿貌嶷然，深沉有器量。

translations.literal: When grown he was honest and upright, with a lofty bearing and deep reserve and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was honest and upright, with a lofty bearing, and possessed depth of character and great capacity.

sentences.zh: 初居洛邑，神武每使入洛，必止嶽舍。

translations.literal: When he first lived in Luoyang, whenever Shenwu sent someone into Luoyang, that person would always lodge at Yue's house.
translations.idiomatic: When he first lived in Luoyang, whenever Gao Huan sent someone into Luoyang, that person would always lodge at Yue's house.

sentences.zh: 岳母山氏嘗夜起，見神武室中無火而有光。

translations.literal: Yue's mother, the Shan clan, once rose at night and saw light in Shenwu's room though there was no fire.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's mother of the Shan clan once rose at night and saw light in Gao Huan's room though there was no fire.

sentences.zh: 移於別室，如前所見。

translations.literal: She moved to another room and saw the same as before.
translations.idiomatic: She moved to another room and saw the same as before.

sentences.zh: 怪之。

translations.literal: She thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: She thought it strange.

sentences.zh: 詣卜者筮，遇《乾》之《大有》。

translations.literal: She went to a diviner to cast the hexagrams and obtained Qian changing to Dazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: She went to a diviner to cast the hexagrams and obtained Qian changing to Dazhuang.

sentences.zh: 占者曰：「吉，《易》稱'飛龍在天，大人造也'，貴不可言。

translations.literal: The diviner said, "Auspicious. The Changes says, 'A flying dragon in heaven—the great man creates,' nobility beyond words."
translations.idiomatic: The diviner said, "Auspicious. The Book of Changes says, 'A flying dragon in heaven—the great man creates,' nobility beyond words."

sentences.zh: 」山氏歸報神武。

translations.literal: The Shan clan returned and reported this to Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Shan clan returned and reported this to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武后起兵於信都，山氏謂嶽曰：「赤光之瑞，今當驗矣，汝可從之。

translations.literal: After Shenwu later raised his army at Xindu, the Shan clan said to Yue, "The omen of red light is now to be fulfilled; you may follow him."
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Huan later raised his army at Xindu, the Shan clan said to Yue, "The omen of red light is now to be fulfilled; you may follow him."

sentences.zh: 」嶽遂往信都，神武見之大悅。

translations.literal: Yue thereupon went to Xindu; Shenwu was greatly pleased to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue thereupon went to Xindu; Gao Huan was greatly pleased to see him.

sentences.zh: 及戰于韓陵，神武將中軍，高昂將左軍，嶽將右軍。

translations.literal: At the battle of Hanling, Shenwu commanded the center army, Gao Ang the left army, and Yue the right army.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Hanling, Gao Huan commanded the center army, Gao Ang the left army, and Yue the right army.

sentences.zh: 中軍敗，嶽舉麾大呼，橫沖賊陣，神武因大破賊。

translations.literal: The center army was defeated; Yue raised his banner and shouted loudly, charging straight across the enemy formation, and Shenwu thereby routed the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The center army was defeated; Yue raised his banner and shouted loudly, charging straight across the enemy formation, and Gao Huan thereby routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 以功除衛將軍、左光祿大夫，封清河郡公。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed General of the Guard and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed General of the Guard and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 母山氏封郡君，授女侍中，入侍皇后。

translations.literal: His mother the Shan clan was enfeoffed as Lady of the Commandery; a daughter was appointed Palace Attendant and entered service to the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: His mother of the Shan clan was enfeoffed as Lady of the Commandery; a daughter was appointed Palace Attendant and entered service to the Empress.

sentences.zh: 天平二年，除侍中、六州軍事都督，尋加開府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianping he was appointed Palace Attendant and Military Commander of Six Provinces, and soon after given an open office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianping he was appointed Palace Attendant and Military Commander of the Six Provinces, and soon after given an open office.

sentences.zh: 岳辟引時賢以為僚屬，論者美之。

translations.literal: Yue recruited men of the time who were worthy to serve as his staff; commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Yue recruited worthy men of the time to serve as his staff; commentators praised this.

sentences.zh: 尋授使持節、六州大都督、冀州大中正。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand Commander of Six Provinces, and Chief Rectifier of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand Commander of the Six Provinces, and Chief Rectifier of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 俄拜京畿大都督，其六州事悉隸京畿。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Grand Commander of the Capital Region, and all affairs of the six provinces were placed under the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was appointed Grand Commander of the Capital Region, and all affairs of the six provinces were placed under the Capital Region.

sentences.zh: 時神武統務晉陽，嶽與侍中孫騰等京師輔政。

translations.literal: At that time Shenwu directed affairs from Jinyang; Yue, together with Palace Attendant Sun Teng and others, assisted government in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Huan directed affairs from Jinyang; Yue, together with Palace Attendant Sun Teng and others, assisted government in the capital.

sentences.zh: 嶽性至孝，母疾，衣不解帶。

translations.literal: Yue was supremely filial; when his mother was ill he did not unfasten his belt.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was supremely filial; when his mother was ill he did not unfasten his belt even to sleep.

sentences.zh: 及遭喪去職，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: When he encountered mourning he left office; his grief wasted him to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: When he encountered mourning he left office; his grief wasted him to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 神武憂之，每日遣人勞勉。

translations.literal: Shenwu worried for him and every day sent someone to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan worried for him and every day sent someone to comfort and encourage him.

sentences.zh: 尋起復本位，曆冀、晉二州刺史、西南道大都督，有綏邊之稱。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to his former post; he served as Governor of Ji and Jin provinces and Grand Commander of the Southwest Circuit, and was called one who pacified the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to his former post; he served as Governor of Ji and Jin provinces and Grand Commander of the Southwest Circuit, and was acclaimed for pacifying the frontier.

sentences.zh: 及神武崩，侯景叛，梁武乘間遣其貞陽侯明於寒山，擁泗水灌彭城，與景為掎角聲援。

translations.literal: When Shenwu died, Hou Jing rebelled; Emperor Wu of Liang seized the opportunity and sent his Marquis of Zhenyang Ming to Han Mountain, damming the Si River to flood Pengcheng, coordinating with Jing in pincer support.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan died, Hou Jing rebelled; Emperor Wu of Liang seized the opportunity and sent his Marquis of Zhenyang Ming to Han Mountain, damming the Si River to flood Pengcheng, coordinating with Jing in mutual support.

sentences.zh: 岳總諸軍南討，與行台慕容紹宗擊破明，禽之。

translations.literal: Yue commanded all armies in the southern campaign and, together with the Mobile Headquarters Murong Shaozong, defeated Ming and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue commanded all armies in the southern campaign and, together with the Mobile Headquarters Murong Shaozong, defeated Ming and captured him.

sentences.zh: 景仍于渦陽與左衛將軍劉豐等相持。

translations.literal: Jing still held at Woyang against Left Guard General Liu Feng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Jing still held at Woyang against Left Guard General Liu Feng and others.

sentences.zh: 嶽又破之。

translations.literal: Yue again defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue again defeated him.

sentences.zh: 以功除太尉。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 又統慕容紹宗、劉豐等攻王思政於長社。

translations.literal: He also commanded Murong Shaozong, Liu Feng, and others in attacking Wang Sizheng at Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: He also commanded Murong Shaozong, Liu Feng, and others in attacking Wang Sizheng at Changshe.

sentences.zh: 岳引洧水灌城。

translations.literal: Yue led the Wei River to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yue led the Wei River to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 紹宗、劉豐為思政所獲。

translations.literal: Shaozong and Liu Feng were captured by Sizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong and Liu Feng were captured by Sizheng.

sentences.zh: 西魏出兵援思政，嶽內外防禦，城不沒者三板。

translations.literal: Western Wei sent troops to aid Sizheng; Yue defended within and without, and the city was submerged only three boards short of the top.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei sent troops to aid Sizheng; Yue defended within and without, and the city was submerged only three boards short of the top.

sentences.zh: 會文襄親臨，數日克城，獲思政等。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang came in person, the city was taken within days and Sizheng and others were captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wenxiang came in person, the city was taken within days and Sizheng and others were captured.

sentences.zh: 以功別封真定縣男。

translations.literal: For his merit he was separately enfeoffed as Baron of Zhending County.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was separately enfeoffed as Baron of Zhending County.

sentences.zh: 文襄以為己功，故賞典不弘。

translations.literal: Wenxiang regarded it as his own achievement, so the rewards were not generous.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang regarded it as his own achievement, so the rewards were not generous.

sentences.zh: 文襄崩，文宣出撫晉陽，令嶽以本官兼尚書左僕射，留鎮鄴。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang died, Wenxuan went out to comfort Jinyang and ordered Yue to retain his former office while also serving as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, remaining to guard Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang died, Wenxuan went out to comfort Jinyang and ordered Yue to retain his former office while also serving as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, remaining to guard Ye.

sentences.zh: 天保初，進封清河郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao his rank was advanced to Prince of Qinghe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao his rank was advanced to Prince of Qinghe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 五年，加太保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 為西南道大行台，統司徒潘相樂等救江陵。

translations.literal: He served as Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Southwest Circuit, commanding Minister of Works Pan Xiangyue and others to rescue Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Southwest Circuit, commanding Minister of Works Pan Xiangyue and others to rescue Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 師次義陽，西魏克荊州。

translations.literal: The army halted at Yiyang; Western Wei captured Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Yiyang; Western Wei captured Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 因略地，克郢州，獲梁郢州刺史陸法和，送鄴。

translations.literal: They thereupon seized territory, captured Ying Province, took Liang's Governor of Ying Lu Fazhi, and sent him to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon seized territory, captured Ying Province, took Liang's Governor of Ying Lu Fazhi, and sent him to Ye.

sentences.zh: 詔岳旋師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yue to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yue to withdraw the army.

sentences.zh: 嶽自討寒山、長社，及出隨、陸，並有功，威名彌重。

translations.literal: From his campaigns at Han Mountain and Changshe to his expeditions in Sui and Lu, Yue had merit in all; his fame and prestige grew ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: From his campaigns at Han Mountain and Changshe to his expeditions in Sui and Lu, Yue had merit in all; his fame and prestige grew ever heavier.

sentences.zh: 性華侈，尤悅酒色，歌姬舞女，陳鼎擊鐘，諸王皆莫及。

translations.literal: By nature he was luxurious; he especially delighted in wine and women, with singing girls and dancing women, setting out cauldrons and striking bells—none of the princes could match him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was luxurious; he especially delighted in wine and women, with singing girls and dancing women, setting out cauldrons and striking bells—none of the princes could match him.

sentences.zh: 初，高歸彥少孤，神武令嶽撫養。

translations.literal: Initially, when Gao Guiyan was orphaned young, Shenwu had Yue raise him.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Gao Guiyan was orphaned young, Gao Huan had Yue raise him.

sentences.zh: 輕其年幼，情禮甚薄，歸彥內銜之。

translations.literal: Yue looked down on him for his youth and showed him very little affection; Guiyan harbored resentment within.
translations.idiomatic: Yue looked down on him for his youth and showed him very little affection; Guiyan harbored resentment within.

sentences.zh: 及歸彥為領軍，嶽謂其德己，更倚仗之。

translations.literal: When Guiyan became Commander of the Palace Guard, Yue thought he owed him a debt and relied on him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Guiyan became Commander of the Palace Guard, Yue thought he owed him a debt and relied on him all the more.

sentences.zh: 歸彥密構其短，奏岳造城南大宅，僭擬為永巷，但無闕耳。

translations.literal: Guiyan secretly framed him and memorialized that Yue had built a great mansion south of the city, modeling it on the Eternal Lane, lacking only the gate-towers.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan secretly framed him and memorialized that Yue had built a great mansion south of the city, modeling it on the Eternal Lane, lacking only the gate-towers.

sentences.zh: 帝后夜行，見壯麗，意不平。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress walked at night, saw its grandeur, and were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress walked at night, saw its grandeur, and were displeased.

sentences.zh: 仍屬帝召鄴下婦人薛氏入宮，而嶽先嘗迎之，至宅，由其姊也。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor was to summon a woman of Ye named Xue into the palace; Yue had earlier welcomed her to his residence because she was his elder sister's kin.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the emperor was to summon a woman of Ye named Xue into the palace; Yue had earlier welcomed her to his residence because she was his elder sister's kin.

sentences.zh: 帝縣薛氏姊而鋸殺之，讓嶽，以為奸人女。

translations.literal: The emperor had Xue's elder sister strung up and sawed to death, reproached Yue, and said she was the daughter of an adulterer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Xue's elder sister strung up and sawed to death, reproached Yue, and said she was the daughter of an adulterer.

sentences.zh: 嶽曰：「臣本欲取之，嫌其輕薄，非奸也。

translations.literal: Yue said, "Your servant originally wished to take her but disliked her frivolity; she was not an adulteress."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Your servant originally wished to take her but disliked her frivolity; she was not an adulteress."

sentences.zh: 」帝益怒，使高歸彥就宅賜以鴆。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier still and had Gao Guiyan go to the residence and bestow poison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier still and had Gao Guiyan go to the residence and bestow poison.

sentences.zh: 嶽曰：「臣無罪。

translations.literal: Yue said, "Your servant is without crime."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Your servant is without crime."

sentences.zh: 」彥曰：「飲之！

translations.literal: Guiyan said, "Drink it!"
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan said, "Drink it!"

sentences.zh: 」飲而薨。

translations.literal: He drank and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drank and died.

sentences.zh: 朝野惜之，時年三十四。

translations.literal: Court and country mourned him; he was thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country mourned him; he was thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 詔大鴻臚護喪事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈太宰、太傅、假黃鉞、給轀輬車，諡曰昭武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Grand Tutor, granted the ceremonial yellow axe and an imperial carriage, with the posthumous title Zhaowu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Grand Tutor, granted the ceremonial yellow axe and an imperial carriage, with the posthumous title Zhaowu.

sentences.zh: 敕以城南宅為莊嚴寺。

translations.literal: An edict turned the mansion south of the city into Zhuangyan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: An edict turned the mansion south of the city into Zhuangyan Temple.

sentences.zh: 初，岳與神武經綸天下，家有私兵戎器，儲甲千餘領。

translations.literal: Initially, when Yue and Shenwu were ordering the realm, his household had private soldiers and weapons, storing more than a thousand suits of armor.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Yue and Gao Huan were ordering the realm, his household had private soldiers and weapons, storing more than a thousand suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 文襄末，嶽表求納之，文襄推心相任，不許。

translations.literal: Near the end of Wenxiang's reign Yue memorialized asking to turn them in; Wenxiang trusted him wholeheartedly and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Wenxiang's reign Yue memorialized asking to turn them in; Wenxiang trusted him wholeheartedly and did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 文宣時，亦頻請納，又不許。

translations.literal: In Wenxuan's time he also repeatedly asked to turn them in, and again it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenxuan's time he also repeatedly asked to turn them in, and again it was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 將薨，遺表謝恩，並請上甲。

translations.literal: When he was about to die he left a final memorial thanking for grace and also asking to present the armor.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to die he left a final memorial thanking for grace and also asking to present the armor.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，方許納焉。

translations.literal: Only after the burial was permission given to turn it in.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the burial was permission given to turn it in.

sentences.zh: 皇建中，配享文襄廟庭。

translations.literal: In the Huangjian era he was granted a place in the sacrifices at Wenxiang's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangjian era he was granted a place in the sacrifices at Wenxiang's temple.

sentences.zh: 後歸彥反，武成知其前譖，以歸彥良賤百口贈岳家。

translations.literal: Later when Guiyan rebelled, Wucheng knew of his earlier slander and gave a hundred mouths of Guiyan's good and base followers to Yue's family.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Guiyan rebelled, Wucheng knew of his earlier slander and gave a hundred mouths of Guiyan's good and base followers to Yue's family.

sentences.zh: 贈岳太師、太保，餘如故。

translations.literal: Yue was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian; the rest remained as before.

sentences.zh: 子勱。

translations.literal: His son Mo.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mo.

sentences.zh: 勱字敬德，幼聰敏，美風儀，以仁孝聞。

translations.literal: Mo, styled Jingde, was clever from childhood, with fine bearing, and was known for benevolence and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, whose style name was Jingde, was clever from childhood, with fine bearing, and was known for benevolence and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 七歲襲爵清河王，十四為青州刺史。

translations.literal: At seven he succeeded to the title of Prince of Qinghe; at fourteen he became Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he succeeded to the title of Prince of Qinghe; at fourteen he became Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 曆祠部尚書、開府儀同三司，改封安樂侯。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, Commissioner with the same powers as the Three Excellencies and an open office, and was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, Commissioner with the same powers as the Three Excellencies and an open office, and was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Anle.

sentences.zh: 性剛直，有才幹。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and firm and possessed talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and firm and possessed talent and ability.

sentences.zh: 斛律光雅敬之，每征伐則引為副。

translations.literal: Hulü Guang greatly respected him and on every campaign took him as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Guang greatly respected him and on every campaign took him as deputy.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及後主為周師所敗，勱奉太后歸鄴。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord was defeated by Zhou troops, Mo escorted the Empress Dowager back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord was defeated by Zhou troops, Mo escorted the Empress Dowager back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 進宦官放縱，儀同苟子溢尤幸。

translations.literal: Eunuchs were allowed to run wild; Yitong Gou Ziyi was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs were allowed to run wild; Yitong Gou Ziyi was especially favored.

sentences.zh: 勱將斬以徇，太后救之，乃得釋。

translations.literal: Mo was about to execute him as an example; the Empress Dowager saved him, and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was about to execute him as an example; the Empress Dowager saved him, and he was released.

sentences.zh: 劉文殊竊謂勱曰：「子溢之徒，言成禍福，何得如此！

translations.literal: Liu Wenshu privately said to Mo, "Ziyi and his sort make words into fortune and calamity—how can you act thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenshu privately said to Mo, "Ziyi and his sort make words into fortune and calamity—how can you act thus!"

sentences.zh: 」勱攘袂曰：「今西軍日侵，朝貴多叛，正由此輩弄權。

translations.literal: Mo rolled up his sleeves and said, "Now the western army advances daily and many court nobles rebel—it is precisely because this crowd manipulates power."
translations.idiomatic: Mo rolled up his sleeves and said, "Now the western army advances daily and many court nobles rebel—it is precisely because this crowd manipulates power."

sentences.zh: 若今日殺之，明日就誅，無恨。

translations.literal: If I kill them today, even if I am executed tomorrow, I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: If I kill them today, even if I am executed tomorrow, I have no regret."

sentences.zh: 」文殊甚愧之。

translations.literal: Wenshu was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 勱勸後主，五品已下家略，悉置三臺上，脅之曰：「若戰不捷，則燒之。

translations.literal: Mo advised the Later Lord that households of fifth rank and below in the capital should all be placed on the Three Platforms, and threatened them, saying, "If the battle is not won, they will be burned."
translations.idiomatic: Mo advised the Later Lord that households of fifth rank and below in the capital should all be placed on the Three Platforms, and threatened them, saying, "If the battle is not won, they will be burned."

sentences.zh: 此輩必死戰，乃可捷也。

translations.literal: This crowd will fight to the death, and only then can victory be won."
translations.idiomatic: This crowd will fight to the death, and only then can victory be won."

sentences.zh: 」後主不從，遂棄鄴東遷。

translations.literal: The Later Lord did not follow this and abandoned Ye to flee east.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord did not follow this and abandoned Ye to flee east.

sentences.zh: 勱恆後殿，為周軍所得。

translations.literal: Mo always brought up the rear and was captured by Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mo always brought up the rear and was captured by Zhou troops.

sentences.zh: 武帝與語，大悅，因問齊亡所由，勱發言流涕，悲不自勝，帝為改容。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou spoke with him and was greatly pleased; he asked the cause of Qi's fall, and Mo spoke until he wept, overcome with grief; the emperor changed his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou spoke with him and was greatly pleased; he asked the cause of Qi's fall, and Mo spoke until he wept, overcome with grief; the emperor changed his expression.

sentences.zh: 授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commissioner with the same powers as the Three Excellencies and an open office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commissioner with the same powers as the Three Excellencies and an open office.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，謂曰：「齊亡由任邪佞，公父子忠良，聞於鄰境，宜善自愛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor he said to him, "Qi fell because wicked and flattering men were employed; you father and son are loyal and good, known in neighboring states—you should take good care of yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor he said to him, "Qi fell because wicked and flattering men were employed; you father and son are loyal and good, known in neighboring states—you should take good care of yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」勱拜謝曰：「勱，亡齊末屬，不能扶危定傾，既蒙獲宥，已多優幸，況濫叨名級，致速官謗。

translations.literal: Mo bowed in thanks and said, "Mo is a remnant subject of fallen Qi and could not shore up peril and right the tipping vessel. Having received pardon, I already enjoy excessive favor; how much more if I presumptuously accept rank and title and hasten official censure."
translations.idiomatic: Mo bowed in thanks and said, "Mo is a remnant subject of fallen Qi and could not shore up peril and right the tipping vessel. Having received pardon, I already enjoy excessive favor; how much more if I presumptuously accept rank and title and hasten official censure."

sentences.zh: 」帝甚器之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 再遷楚州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Governor of Chu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to Governor of Chu Province.

sentences.zh: 城北有伍子胥廟，其俗敬鬼，祈者必以牛酒，至破產業。

translations.literal: North of the city was a temple to Wu Zixu; the local custom revered ghosts, and those who prayed had to offer cattle and wine, even to the ruin of their households.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city was a temple to Wu Zixu; the local custom revered ghosts, and those who prayed had to offer cattle and wine, even to the ruin of their households.

sentences.zh: 勱歎曰：「子胥賢者，豈宜損百姓乎！

translations.literal: Mo sighed and said, "Zixu was a worthy man—how could he be made to harm the common people!"
translations.idiomatic: Mo sighed and said, "Zixu was a worthy man—how could he be made to harm the common people!"

sentences.zh: 」告諭所部，自是遂止。

translations.literal: He announced this to his jurisdiction, and from then on it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He announced this to his jurisdiction, and from then on it ceased.

sentences.zh: 百姓賴之。

translations.literal: The common people relied upon him.
translations.idiomatic: The people came to depend on him.

sentences.zh: 開皇七年，轉光州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaihuang, he was transferred to Governor of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaihuang, he was made Governor of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 上表曰：「陳氏數年已來，荒悖滋甚，天厭亂德，妖實人興。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying, "In recent years the Chen house has grown ever more lawless and perverse; Heaven has grown weary of chaotic virtue, and portents have truly risen through human agency.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "In recent years the Chen regime has grown ever more lawless and corrupt; Heaven has turned against their disorder, and omens have sprung up through human folly.

sentences.zh: 或空裏時有大聲，或行路共傳鬼怪，或刳人肝以祠天狗，或自捨身以厭妖訛。

translations.literal: At times great sounds were heard from empty air; on the roads people spread tales of ghosts and monsters; some gouged out human livers to sacrifice to the Heavenly Dog; some gave up their own lives to suppress demonic falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes thunderous voices rang from empty sky; travelers traded rumors of ghosts and monsters; some gouged out livers to offer to the Heavenly Dog; others sacrificed themselves to ward off demonic delusions.

sentences.zh: 人神怨憤，怪異薦發。

translations.literal: Men and spirits alike were aggrieved and enraged, and strange things arose one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth seethed with resentment, and uncanny events broke out in succession.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸才，猥蒙朝寄，頻曆蕃守，與其鄰接。

translations.literal: Your servant, with mediocre talent, has undeservedly received the court's trust, repeatedly serving as frontier governor and bordering upon them.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of modest ability who has undeservedly received the court's commission, having served repeatedly on the frontier where our lands adjoin theirs.

sentences.zh: 密邇仇仇，知其動靜。

translations.literal: Closely bordering the hostile state, I know their movements.
translations.idiomatic: Living right on Chen's border, I know their every move.

sentences.zh: 天討有罪，此即其時。

translations.literal: Heaven's punishment falls upon the guilty—this is the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's judgment is upon the guilty—now is the time to strike.

sentences.zh: 若戎車雷動，戈船電邁，臣雖駑怯，請效鷹犬。

translations.literal: If war chariots roll like thunder and armored ships flash like lightning, though your servant is dull and timid, I beg to serve as hawk and hound.
translations.idiomatic: When the war chariots thunder forth and the warships race like lightning, though I am slow and faint-hearted, I ask only to serve as your hunting hawk and hound.

sentences.zh: 」並上平陳五策，帝嘉之，答以優詔。

translations.literal: " He also submitted five strategies for pacifying Chen; the emperor commended him and replied with an edict of special favor.
translations.idiomatic: " He also submitted five plans for conquering Chen. The emperor praised him and answered with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，以勱為行軍總管，從宜陽公王世積下陳江州，以功拜上開府，賜物三千段。

translations.literal: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Mo was made Campaign Commander-in-Chief; following Yiyang Duke Wang Shiji, he descended upon Chen's Jiang Province, and for his merit was appointed Superlative Opening Grandee and granted three thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire launched its full assault on Chen, Mo was appointed campaign commander-in-chief. Following Yiyang Duke Wang Shiji, he drove down into Chen's Jiang Province; for his service he was made Superlative Opening Grandee and rewarded with three thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 時隴右諸羌，數為寇亂。

translations.literal: At that time the Qiang of Longyou repeatedly raided and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Qiang tribes of Longyou were constantly raiding and causing disorder.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以勱有威名，拜洮州刺史。

translations.literal: Because Mo had a reputation for stern authority, the court appointed him Governor of Tao Province.
translations.idiomatic: The court, knowing Mo's reputation for stern authority, appointed him Governor of Tao Province.

sentences.zh: 下車大崇威惠，人夷悅附，豪猾屏跡，路不拾遺，以善政稱。

translations.literal: Upon taking office he greatly emphasized both authority and kindness; Chinese and barbarians alike gladly submitted, the powerful and cunning vanished from sight, and none picked up what others dropped on the road—he was known for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he took office he combined firm authority with generous kindness. Chinese and tribesmen alike gladly submitted, local bullies disappeared, and people no longer bothered to pick up lost goods on the road—his rule became a byword for good government.

sentences.zh: 後吐谷渾來寇，勱時遇疾，不能拒戰，賊遂大掠而去。

translations.literal: Later Tuyuhun came raiding; Mo was then ill and could not resist in battle, and the bandits plundered on a great scale before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tuyuhun invaded while Mo lay ill and unable to fight; the raiders looted the region extensively before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 憲司奏勱亡戶口，坐免，卒於家。

translations.literal: The censorate memorialized that Mo had lost population; he was dismissed from office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate reported that Mo had failed to protect his people; he was removed from office and died at home.

sentences.zh: 大唐褒顯前代名臣，追贈都督四州諸軍事、定州刺史。

translations.literal: The Great Tang, honoring eminent ministers of former ages, posthumously enfeoffed him as Commander-in-Chief over the military affairs of four provinces and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang later honored distinguished ministers of earlier dynasties, Mo was posthumously granted the title of Commander-in-Chief over four provinces and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子士廉最知名。

translations.literal: His son Shilian was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shilian became the best known of his children.

sentences.zh: 廣平公盛，神武從叔祖也。

translations.literal: Duke of Guangping, Sheng, was a granduncle on Shenwu's mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Guangping, Sheng, was Shenwu's granduncle on the maternal line.

sentences.zh: 寬厚有長者風。

translations.literal: He was generous and mild, with the bearing of an elder of stature.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous and mild, with the dignified bearing of a true elder.

sentences.zh: 神武起兵於信都，盛來赴，以為中軍大都督，封廣平郡公。

translations.literal: When Shenwu raised his army at Xindu, Sheng came to join him and was made Grand Commander of the Central Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Guangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu raised his army at Xindu, Sheng rallied to his side and was appointed Grand Commander of the Central Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Guangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 歷位司徒、太尉。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Minister over the Masses and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to serve as Minister over the Masses and Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 天平三年，薨於位，贈假黃鉞、太尉、太師、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianping he died in office; he was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, the titles of Grand Commandant and Grand Preceptor, and the duty of recording affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianping he died in office and was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, the titles of Grand Commandant and Grand Preceptor, and the post of Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 無子，以兄子子瑗嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, his elder brother's son Ziyuan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons, so his elder brother's son Ziyuan inherited his line.

sentences.zh: 天保初，改封平昌王，卒于魏尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao his fief was changed to Prince of Pingchang; he died in the capital of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianbao reign his title was changed to Prince of Pingchang, and he died in the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 陽州公永樂，神武從祖兄子也。

translations.literal: Duke of Yangzhou, Yongle, was the son of Shenwu's granduncle's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Yangzhou, Yongle, was the son of Shenwu's granduncle's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，封陽州縣伯，進爵為公，累遷北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangzhou County, advanced in rank to duke, and successively promoted to Governor of Northern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taichang he was made Marquis of Yangzhou County, later raised to duke, and eventually rose to Governor of Northern Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 河橋之戰，司徒高昂失利奔退，永樂守洛陽南城。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Heqiao, Minister over the Masses Gao Ang suffered defeat and fled; Yongle held the southern city of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Heqiao, Minister over the Masses Gao Ang was defeated and fled, while Yongle held the southern quarter of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 昂走趣城南，西軍追者將至，永樂不開門，昂遂為西軍所禽。

translations.literal: Ang fled toward the southern city; the western army's pursuers were about to arrive, but Yongle would not open the gate, and Ang was thereupon captured by the western army.
translations.idiomatic: Ang ran for the southern city as the western army closed in, but Yongle refused to open the gates, and Ang was captured by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 神武大怒，杖之二百。

translations.literal: Shenwu was furious and had him beaten two hundred strokes with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu flew into a rage and had him beaten two hundred strokes with the staff.

sentences.zh: 後罷豫州，家產不立。

translations.literal: Later he was removed from Yu Province, and his household wealth never prospered.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was removed from Yu Province and never managed to build up his family fortune.

sentences.zh: 神武問其故，對曰：「裴監為長史，辛公正為別駕，受王委寄，鬥酒只雞不敢入。

translations.literal: Shenwu asked the reason, and he replied, "Pei Jian served as Chief Administrator and Xin Gongzheng as Vice Governor; entrusted by Your Highness, they would not accept even a cup of wine or a single chicken."
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu asked why, and he answered, "Pei Jian was chief administrator and Xin Gongzheng was vice governor. Entrusted by Your Highness, they would not accept even the smallest gift."

sentences.zh: 」神武乃以永樂為濟州，仍以監、公正為長史、別駕。

translations.literal: Shenwu thereupon made Yongle Governor of Ji Province and again appointed Jian and Gongzheng as Chief Administrator and Vice Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu then made Yongle Governor of Ji Province and reappointed Jian and Gongzheng as chief administrator and vice governor.

sentences.zh: 謂永樂曰：「爾勿大貪，小小義取莫復畏。

translations.literal: He said to Yongle, "Do not be too greedy; take a little on grounds of propriety and need not fear."
translations.idiomatic: He told Yongle, "Do not be too greedy—but a modest taking on grounds of propriety need not worry you."

sentences.zh: 」永樂至州，監、公正諫不見聽，以狀啟神武。

translations.literal: When Yongle reached the province, Jian and Gongzheng remonstrated but he would not listen; they reported the matter in a memorial to Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongle arrived in the province, Jian and Gongzheng protested, but he ignored them and they reported his conduct to Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 神武封啟以示永樂，然後知二人清直，並擢用之。

translations.literal: Shenwu sealed their memorial and showed it to Yongle; only then did he realize the two men were upright and incorruptible, and both were promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu sealed their report and showed it to Yongle, who then realized how upright and honest the two men were; both were promoted and given greater responsibility.

sentences.zh: 永樂卒於州，贈太師、太尉、錄尚書事，諡曰武昭。

translations.literal: Yongle died in the province and was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Preceptor and Grand Commandant and the duty of recording affairs of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous title was Wuzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle died in office and was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Preceptor and Grand Commandant and the post of Recorder of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous name was Wuzhao.

sentences.zh: 無子，從兄思宗以第二子孝緒為後，襲爵。

translations.literal: Having no son, his elder clansman Sizong's second son Xiaoxu was made his heir and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons, so his elder clansman Sizong's second son Xiaoxu was adopted as heir and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 天保初，改封脩城郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao his fief was changed to Prince of Xiucheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianbao reign his title was changed to Prince of Xiucheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 永樂弟長弼，小名阿伽。

translations.literal: Yongle's younger brother Changbi had the childhood name Aga.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle's younger brother Changbi went by the childhood name Aga.

sentences.zh: 性粗武，出入城市，好毆擊行路，時人皆呼為阿伽郎君。

translations.literal: By nature he was rough and martial; going in and out of cities, he liked to beat people on the road, and at the time everyone called him Lord Aga.
translations.idiomatic: He was rough and violent by nature and liked to assault passersby in the streets; people called him Lord Aga.

sentences.zh: 以宗室封廣武王。

translations.literal: By virtue of his imperial clan status he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: As a member of the imperial clan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 時有天恩道人，至凶暴，橫行閭肆，後入長弼黨，專以鬥為事。

translations.literal: At the time there was a Daoist priest named Tian'en who was extremely brutal and rampaged through the lanes; later he joined Changbi's faction and devoted himself entirely to brawling.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Daoist called Tian'en, a man of extreme violence who terrorized the streets; he later joined Changbi's circle and lived only for fighting.

sentences.zh: 文宣並收掩付獄，天恩等十餘人皆棄市，長弼鞭一百。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan had them all seized and imprisoned; Tian'en and more than ten others were executed in the marketplace, and Changbi was flogged one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan had them arrested; Tian'en and more than ten others were executed in public, and Changbi was flogged one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 尋為南營州刺史，在州無故自驚走。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made Governor of Southern Ying Province; while in office he fled for no apparent reason in sudden panic.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Governor of Southern Ying Province, but while in office he suddenly panicked and fled for no clear reason.

sentences.zh: 叛亡入突厥，竟不知死所。

translations.literal: He defected and fled into the Turks, and in the end no one knew where he died.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to the Turks as a defector, and no one ever learned where he died.

sentences.zh: 上洛王思宗，神武從子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Shangluo, Sizong, was Shenwu's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shangluo, Sizong, was Shenwu's nephew.

sentences.zh: 性寬和，頗有武幹。

translations.literal: By nature he was mild and harmonious and possessed considerable martial ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle and even-tempered by nature, yet showed real talent for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封上洛郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shangluo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianbao reign he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shangluo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 歷位司空、太傅，薨於官。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Minister of Works and Grand Tutor and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Works and Grand Tutor in turn and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子元海，累遷散騎常侍，願處山林，修行釋典，文宣許之。

translations.literal: His son Yuanhai was successively promoted to Attendant Cavalier in Regular Attendance; he wished to dwell in mountain forests and cultivate Buddhist scriptures, and Emperor Wenxuan granted this.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanhai rose to Attendant Cavalier in Regular Attendance, but wished to retire to the mountains and devote himself to Buddhist scripture; Emperor Wenxuan allowed it.

sentences.zh: 乃入林慮山，經二年，絕棄人事。

translations.literal: He thereupon entered Mount Linlu and for two years utterly abandoned worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Mount Linlu and for two years cut himself off entirely from the world.

sentences.zh: 志不能固，自啟求歸。

translations.literal: His resolve could not hold firm, and he petitioned on his own to return.
translations.idiomatic: His resolve failed him, and he asked permission to come back.

sentences.zh: 徵復本任，便縱酒肆情，廣納姬侍。

translations.literal: Recalled to his former post, he at once gave himself over to wine and indulged his desires, widely taking concubines and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to his old office, he immediately abandoned restraint, drinking freely and taking concubines in great number.

sentences.zh: 又除領軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was again appointed General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 器小志大，頗以智謀自許。

translations.literal: Small in capacity but large in ambition, he rather prided himself on clever stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Petty in talent but grand in ambition, he fancied himself a master of intrigue.

sentences.zh: 皇建末，孝昭幸晉陽，武成居守，元海以散騎常侍留典機密。

translations.literal: At the end of the Huangjian reign, when Emperor Xiaozhao visited Jinyang and Wucheng remained to guard the capital, Yuanhai stayed behind as Attendant Cavalier in Regular Attendance to manage confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Huangjian, when Emperor Xiaozhao went to Jinyang and Wucheng stayed behind to guard the capital, Yuanhai remained as Attendant Cavalier in Regular Attendance in charge of confidential matters.

sentences.zh: 初，孝昭之誅楊愔等，謂武成雲，事成，以汝為皇太弟。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiaozhao executed Yang Yin and the others, he had told Wucheng, "When the affair succeeds, I shall make you Imperial Younger Brother."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao had Yang Yin and his allies killed, he had promised Wucheng, "When this succeeds, I will make you Imperial Younger Brother."

sentences.zh: 及踐位，乃使武成在鄴主兵，立子百年為皇太子，武成甚不平。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he instead had Wucheng remain at Ye to command troops, made his son Bainian crown prince, and Wucheng was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the throne, however, he kept Wucheng at Ye in command of troops, made his own son Bainian crown prince, and Wucheng was deeply aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 先是，恆留濟南於鄴，除領軍厙狄伏連為幽州刺史，以斛律豐樂為領軍，以分武成之權。

translations.literal: Previously he had always kept Jinan at Ye; he appointed General of the Palace Guard Ku Di Fulin Governor of You Province and made Hu Lü Fengle General of the Palace Guard, so as to divide Wucheng's power.
translations.idiomatic: He had long kept Prince Jinan at Ye, appointed Palace Guard General Ku Di Fulin Governor of You Province, and made Hu Lü Fengle the new Palace Guard General to split Wucheng's authority.

sentences.zh: 武成留伏連而不聽豐樂視事。

translations.literal: Wucheng detained Fulin and would not allow Fengle to assume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng kept Fulin at his side and refused to let Fengle take up office.

sentences.zh: 乃與河陽王孝瑜偽獵，謀於野，暗乃歸。

translations.literal: He then went on a sham hunt with Prince of Heyang Xiaoyu, plotted in the wilds, and returned secretly by night.
translations.idiomatic: He then staged a hunting expedition with Prince of Heyang Xiaoyu, plotted with him in the open country, and slipped back under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 先是童謠云：「中興寺內白鳧翁，四方側聽聲雍雍，道人聞之夜打鐘。

translations.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme said, "In Zhongxing Temple, the white duck old man; from the four quarters all listen—his voice is harmonious; the Daoist hears it and beats the bell at night."
