translations.idiomatic: A children's rhyme had earlier run, "In Zhongxing Temple, the white duck old man; from every side they listen—his voice is deep and clear; the Daoist hears it and the bell is struck at night."

sentences.zh: 」時丞相府在北城中，即舊中興寺也；

translations.literal: At that time the Chancellor's office was in the northern city, which was the old Zhongxing Temple;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the chancellor's residence stood in the northern city—the site of the old Zhongxing Temple;

sentences.zh: 鳧翁謂雄雞，蓋指武成小字步落稽也；

translations.literal: "duck old man" referred to the cock, and pointed to Wucheng's childhood name Buluoqi;
translations.idiomatic: "duck old man" meant the cock, and referred to Wucheng's childhood name Buluoqi;

sentences.zh: 道人，濟南王小名也；

translations.literal: "the Daoist" was Prince Jinan's childhood name;
translations.idiomatic: "the Daoist" was Prince Jinan's childhood name;

sentences.zh: 打鐘，言將被擊也。

translations.literal: "beats the bell" meant that he was about to be struck down.
translations.idiomatic: "beats the bell" meant that he would soon be attacked.

sentences.zh: 既而太史奏言，北城有天子氣，昭帝以為濟南應之，乃使平秦王歸彥之鄴，迎濟南赴并州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the court astronomers memorialized that there was an imperial aura in the northern city; Emperor Zhao thought Jinan corresponded to it and sent Prince of Pingqin Guiyan to Ye to escort Jinan to Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court astronomers reported an imperial aura over the northern city; Emperor Zhao believed Jinan was the omen's subject and sent Prince of Pingqin Guiyan to Ye to bring Jinan to Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 武成先告元海，並問自安之計。

translations.literal: Wucheng first informed Yuanhai and also asked him for a plan to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng confided in Yuanhai first and asked how he might save himself.

sentences.zh: 元海曰：「皇太后萬福，至尊孝性非常，殿下不須別慮。

translations.literal: Yuanhai said, "The Empress Dowager enjoys boundless fortune, and the Son of Heaven is extraordinarily filial; Your Highness need not worry otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai said, "The Empress Dowager is blessed with long life, and the emperor is profoundly filial—Your Highness has nothing else to fear."

sentences.zh: 」武成曰：「此豈我推誠之意邪？

translations.literal: Wucheng said, "Is this really what I mean by opening my heart to you?"
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng said, "Is that what you call speaking to me in good faith?"

sentences.zh: 」元海乞還省一夜思之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai asked to return to his office and think for one night.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai asked leave to withdraw for one night and think it over.

sentences.zh: 武成即留元海後堂，元海達旦不眠，唯繞床徐步。

translations.literal: Wucheng kept Yuanhai in the rear hall; Yuanhai stayed awake until dawn, pacing slowly around the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng detained him in the rear hall; Yuanhai did not sleep until dawn, pacing slowly around the bed.

sentences.zh: 夜漏未盡，武成遽出曰：「神算如何？

translations.literal: Before the night watch had ended, Wucheng suddenly came out and said, "What does your divine calculation say?"
translations.idiomatic: Before the night was half over, Wucheng came out abruptly and asked, "Well—what does your divine reckoning say?"

sentences.zh: 」答云：「夜中得三策，恐不堪用耳。

translations.literal: He answered, "In the night I obtained three stratagems, but I fear they may not be usable."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I thought of three plans in the night, though I fear none may serve."

sentences.zh: 」因說梁孝王懼誅入關事，請乘數騎入晉陽，先見太后求哀，後見主上，請去兵權，以死為限，求不幹朝政，必保太山之安，此上策也；

translations.literal: He thereupon told the story of Prince Xiao of Liang, who, fearing execution, entered the passes, and urged that Wucheng take a few horsemen into Jinyang, first see the Empress Dowager and beg for mercy, then see the sovereign and request to surrender military authority, taking death as his limit and asking not to interfere in court affairs—this would surely secure the safety of Mount Tai; this was the upper stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: He then cited Prince Xiao of Liang, who had fled into the passes fearing death, and urged Wucheng to ride into Jinyang with a small escort, first throw himself on the Empress Dowager's mercy, then ask the emperor to strip him of military power, swear to keep out of politics, and accept death if need be—thus securing safety as firm as Mount Tai; that was the best plan;

sentences.zh: 若不然，當具表雲威權大盛，恐取謗眾口，請青、齊二州刺史，沉靖自居，必不招物議，此中策也。

translations.literal: if not, he should submit a memorial saying his authority was too great and he feared slander from the multitude, and request the governorships of Qing and Qi Provinces, living quietly and modestly—this would surely draw no public criticism; this was the middle stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: If not, he should memorialize that his power had grown too great and invited gossip, and ask to be sent as governor of Qing and Qi Provinces to live quietly—surely drawing no scandal; that was the second plan.

sentences.zh: 更問下策，曰：「發言即恐族誅。

translations.literal: Asked for the lower stratagem, he said, "To speak would risk extermination of the clan."
translations.idiomatic: When pressed for the worst plan, he said, "If I speak, I fear the whole clan will be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 」因逼之，答曰：「濟南世嫡，主上假太后令而奪之，今集文武，示以此敕，執豐樂，斬歸彥，尊濟南，號令天下，以順討逆，此萬世一時也。

translations.literal: Pressed further, he answered, "Jinan is the legitimate heir; the sovereign seized the throne from him on a false order of the Empress Dowager. Now gather civil and military officials, show them this edict, seize Fengle, execute Guiyan, honor Jinan, and command the realm—using obedience to punish rebellion; this is a chance that comes once in ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Pressed again, he said, "Jinan is the rightful heir; the emperor took the throne from him with a forged order from the Empress Dowager. Summon the officials, expose the decree, arrest Fengle, kill Guiyan, restore Jinan, and proclaim him to the empire—righteousness against usurpation. Such a chance comes once in an age."

sentences.zh: 」武成大悅，狐疑，竟未能用。

translations.literal: Wucheng was greatly pleased yet hesitated, and in the end could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng was delighted but wavered, and in the end could not bring himself to act.

sentences.zh: 乃使鄭道謙卜之，皆曰：「不利舉事，靜則吉。

translations.literal: He then had Zheng Daoqian perform divination; all said, "It is unfavorable to raise an affair; if you remain still, it is auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: He had Zheng Daoqian cast the oracle; all the signs said action would fail and stillness would bring fortune.

sentences.zh: 」又召曹魏祖問之國事，對曰：「當有大凶。

translations.literal: He also summoned Cao Weizu and asked about affairs of state; he replied, "There will be great calamity."
translations.idiomatic: He also called in Cao Weizu to ask about the realm; the answer was, "Great disaster awaits."

sentences.zh: 」又時有林慮令姓籓，知占候，密謂武成曰：「宮車當晏駕，殿下為天下王。

translations.literal: At the time there was the magistrate of Linlu, surnamed Fan, who knew divination and secretly told Wucheng, "The imperial carriage will soon halt; Your Highness will become king under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: There was also the magistrate of Linlu, Fan by surname, skilled in divination, who secretly told Wucheng, "The emperor's carriage will soon stop; Your Highness will rule the realm."

sentences.zh: 」武成拘之於內以候之。

translations.literal: Wucheng detained him inside to wait and see.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng kept him confined indoors to see whether the prophecy would come true.

sentences.zh: 又令巫覡卜之，多雲不須舉兵，自有大慶。

translations.literal: He also had shamans perform divination; most said there was no need to raise troops—great good fortune would come of itself.
translations.idiomatic: He had shamans consult the spirits as well; most said he need not mobilize—great fortune would come unbidden.

sentences.zh: 武成乃奉詔，令數百騎送濟南于晉陽。

translations.literal: Wucheng thereupon obeyed the edict and sent several hundred horsemen to escort Jinan to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng then obeyed the order and sent several hundred horsemen to escort Jinan to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 及孝昭崩，武成即位，除元海侍中、開府儀同三司、太子詹事。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao died, Wucheng ascended the throne and appointed Yuanhai Palace Attendant, Grand Master with the same powers as the Three Excellencies and an open office, and Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaozhao's death Wucheng took the throne and made Yuanhai Palace Attendant, Grand Master with the same powers as the Three Excellencies and an open office, and Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 河清二年，元海為和士開譖，被馬鞭六十，責云：「爾在鄴城說我以弟反兄，幾許不義！

translations.literal: In the second year of Heqing, Yuanhai was slandered by He Shikai, was flogged sixty strokes with the horsewhip, and was rebuked with the words, "You in Ye counseled me to have a younger brother rebel against his elder brother—how utterly unrighteous!
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Heqing, He Shikai slandered Yuanhai; he was flogged sixty strokes with the horsewhip and rebuked: "At Ye you urged me to have a younger brother rebel against his elder brother—how shameless!

sentences.zh: 以鄴城兵馬抗并州，幾許無智！

translations.literal: To use Ye's troops and horses to resist Bing Province—how utterly witless!
translations.idiomatic: To raise Ye's armies against Bing Province—how stupid!

sentences.zh: 不義無智，若為可使？

translations.literal: Unrighteous and witless—how can such a man be employed?"
translations.idiomatic: Faithless and foolish—what use is such a man?"

sentences.zh: 」出為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 元海後妻，陸太姬甥也，故尋被追任使。

translations.literal: Yuanhai's later wife was a niece of Empress Lu; therefore before long he was recalled and again given appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai's second wife was a niece of Empress Lu, so he was soon recalled and given office again.

sentences.zh: 武平中，與祖珽共執朝政。

translations.literal: In the Wuping era he shared governance of the court with Zu Ting.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuping era he and Zu Ting jointly controlled the government.

sentences.zh: 元海多乙太姬密語告珽。

translations.literal: Yuanhai often went in secret to Empress Lu and reported confidential words to Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai often visited Empress Lu in private and told Ting what she had confided.

sentences.zh: 珽求領軍，元海不可，珽乃以其所告報太姬。

translations.literal: Ting sought the post of General of the Palace Guard; Yuanhai would not agree, so Ting reported what Yuanhai had told him to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting asked for the post of Palace Guard General, Yuanhai refused; Ting then told the empress everything Yuanhai had relayed.

sentences.zh: 姬怒，出元海為鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: The empress was enraged and sent Yuanhai out as Governor of Zheng Province.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was furious and had Yuanhai sent out as Governor of Zheng Province.

sentences.zh: 鄴城將敗，徵為尚書令。

translations.literal: When Ye was about to fall, he was recalled as Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: As Ye was on the verge of collapse, he was recalled to serve as Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 周建德七年，於鄴城謀逆，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiande of Zhou, he plotted rebellion at Ye and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiande of Northern Zhou, he plotted rebellion at Ye and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 元海好亂樂禍，然詐仁慈，不飲酒啖肉。

translations.literal: Yuanhai delighted in chaos and welcomed calamity, yet he pretended to benevolence, neither drinking wine nor eating meat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai loved turmoil and courted disaster, yet he feigned kindness and abstained from wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 文宣天保末年，敬信內法，乃至宗廟不血食，皆元海所為。

translations.literal: In the late Tianbao years of Emperor Wenxuan, he reverently trusted the inner teachings of the Law, even to the point that the ancestral temple no longer received blood sacrifice—all this was Yuanhai's doing.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Tianbao years of Emperor Wenxuan, he led the court to embrace Buddhism so fervently that even the ancestral temple ceased blood sacrifice—all at Yuanhai's instigation.

sentences.zh: 及為右僕射，又說後主禁屠宰，斷酤酒。

translations.literal: When he became Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, he again persuaded the Later Lord to forbid slaughter and ban the sale of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Once made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, he again urged the Later Lord to forbid slaughter and ban wine sales.

sentences.zh: 然本心非靖，故終致覆敗。

translations.literal: Yet his heart was not tranquil, and so in the end he brought about ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his heart was never at peace, and in the end he brought about his own ruin.

sentences.zh: 思宗弟思好，本浩氏子也，思宗養以為弟，遇之甚薄。

translations.literal: Sizong's younger brother Sihao was originally a son of the Hao clan; Sizong raised him as a younger brother but treated him very poorly.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong's younger brother Sihao was born to the Hao clan; Sizong adopted him as a brother but treated him very harshly.

sentences.zh: 少以騎射事文襄。

translations.literal: In youth he served Wenxiang with horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served Prince Wenxiang as a master of horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 及文宣受命，為左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan received the mandate, Sihao was made General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan received the mandate, Sihao was appointed General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 本名思孝，天保五年討蠕蠕，文宣悅其驍勇，謂曰：「爾擊賊如鶻入鴉群，宜思好事。

translations.literal: His original name was Sixiao. In the fifth year of Tianbao, campaigning against the Rouran, Wenxuan was pleased with his fierce bravery and said, "When you strike the enemy it is like a hawk entering a flock of crows—you should think of doing good deeds."
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Sixiao. In the fifth year of Tianbao, on campaign against the Rouran, Wenxuan praised his fierce bravery and said, "You strike the enemy like a hawk among crows—you ought to turn that spirit to worthy deeds."

sentences.zh: 」故改名焉。

translations.literal: He was therefore renamed.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore given a new name.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書令、朔州道行台、朔州刺史、開府、南安王。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Shuozhou Circuit, Governor of Shuozhou, Commissioner with an open office, and Prince of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Shuozhou Circuit, Governor of Shuozhou, Commissioner with an open office, and Prince of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 甚得邊朔人心。

translations.literal: He won the hearts of the people on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He won the deep loyalty of the northern frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 後主時，斫骨光弁奉使至州，思好迎之甚謹。

translations.literal: In the time of the Later Lord, Zhuogu Guangbian came on a mission to the province; Sihao received him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Later Lord's reign, Zhuogu Guangbian arrived at the province on a mission; Sihao received him with scrupulous courtesy.

sentences.zh: 光弁倨傲，思好因心銜恨。

translations.literal: Guangbian was arrogant; Sihao therefore harbored resentment in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbian behaved arrogantly, and Sihao nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 武平五年，遂舉兵反，與并州諸貴書曰：「主上少長深宮，未辨人之情偽，昵近凶狡，疏遠忠良。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wuping he thereupon raised troops in rebellion and wrote to the nobles of Bing Province, saying, "The sovereign grew up deep within the palace and cannot distinguish true from false in men; he draws near the vicious and crafty and keeps the loyal and good at a distance."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wuping he rose in rebellion and wrote to the Bingzhou nobles, saying, "The sovereign was raised deep in the palace and cannot tell honest men from deceivers; he favors the vicious and estranges the loyal."

sentences.zh: 遂使刀鋸刑餘，貴溢軒階；

translations.literal: Thus castrated men who wield the knife and saw overflow the steps of the hall;
translations.idiomatic: Thus eunuchs and mutilated favorites overflow the palace steps;

sentences.zh: 商胡丑類，擅權帷幄。

translations.literal: ugly classes of Sogdian merchants monopolize power within the curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Sogdian merchants of the vilest sort monopolize power behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 剝削生靈，劫掠朝市，暗於聽受，專行忍害。

translations.literal: They strip the living people, plunder the court and market, are blind in what they hear and accept, and exclusively practice cruel harm.
translations.idiomatic: They strip the people bare, plunder court and market alike, turn a deaf ear to justice, and practice cruelty without restraint.

sentences.zh: 幽母深宮，無復人子之禮；

translations.literal: The mother is shut deep in the palace with no further observance of a son's rites;
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager is immured in the palace, denied even a son's proper rites;

sentences.zh: 二弟殘戮，頓絕孔懷之義。

translations.literal: two younger brothers were slaughtered, abruptly severing the bonds of brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: two imperial brothers were slaughtered, cutting off the ties of kinship.

sentences.zh: 仍縱子立奪馬於東門，光弁制鷹於西市；

translations.literal: They still allow Zili to seize horses at the eastern gate and Guangbian to train hawks in the western market;
translations.idiomatic: They still let Zili seize horses at the eastern gate and Guangbian train hawks in the western market;

sentences.zh: 駁龍得儀同之號，逍遙受郡君之名。

translations.literal: Bolong received the title of Yitong and Xiaoyao received the name of Lady of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bolong was given the rank of Yitong and Xiaoyao the title of Lady of a Commandery.

sentences.zh: 犬馬班位，榮冠軒冕，人不堪役，思長亂階。

translations.literal: Dogs and horses take court rank and glory above the ceremonial caps; the people cannot bear the corvée and long for endless disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Dogs and horses hold court rank above true ministers; the people cannot bear their burdens and hunger for chaos.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王睿，實曰宗英，社稷惟寄。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui is truly the clan's outstanding talent, the charge of the altars and state.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui is truly the clan's finest man, the hope of the realm.

sentences.zh: 左相斛律明月，世為元輔，威著鄰國，並非有辜，奄見誅殄。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Hulü Mingyue, for generations a chief minister, whose authority was felt in neighboring states—both were innocent yet were suddenly executed.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Hulü Mingyue, a chief minister for generations whose fame reached neighboring states—both were guiltless yet were suddenly put to death.

sentences.zh: 孤既忝預皇枝，實蒙殊獎，今便擁率義兵，指除君側之害。

translations.literal: I, unworthy though I am of the imperial branch, have truly received extraordinary favor; now I shall lead righteous troops to remove harm beside the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Though unworthy of the imperial line, I have received extraordinary grace; now I lead righteous troops to purge evil beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 幸悉此懷，無致疑惑。

translations.literal: I hope you will all understand this intent and not harbor doubts."
translations.idiomatic: I trust you will understand my purpose and harbor no doubts."

sentences.zh: 」行台郎王行思之辭也。

translations.literal: The wording was by Wang Xingsi of the Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The letter was composed by Wang Xingsi of the Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 思好至陽曲，自號大丞相，置百官，以行台左丞王尚之為長史。

translations.literal: Sihao reached Yangqu, styled himself Grand Chancellor, established the full bureaucracy, and made Wang Shangzhi, Left Assistant of the Mobile Headquarters, his Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Sihao reached Yangqu, proclaimed himself Grand Chancellor, set up a full bureaucracy, and made Wang Shangzhi, Left Assistant of the Mobile Headquarters, his chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 武衛趙海在晉陽掌兵，時倉卒，不暇奏，矯詔發兵拒之。

translations.literal: Wuwei Zhao Hai was in charge of troops at Jinyang; in the emergency there was no time to memorialize, and he forged an edict to mobilize troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei Zhao Hai commanded troops at Jinyang; in the crisis there was no time for memorials, so he forged an edict and mobilized troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 軍士皆曰：「南安王來，我輩唯須唱萬歲奉迎耳。

translations.literal: The soldiers all said, "The Prince of Nan'an has come—we need only shout ten thousand years and welcome him."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers said, "The Prince of Nan'an is here—we have only to shout long life and welcome him."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞變，使唐邕、莫多婁敬顯、劉桃枝、中領軍厙狄士文馳之晉陽，帝勒兵續進。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of the revolt, he sent Tang Yong, Moduolou Jingxian, Liu Taozhi, and Central Palace Guard Commander Ku Di Shiwen racing to Jinyang; the emperor led troops and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the revolt, the emperor sent Tang Yong, Moduolou Jingxian, Liu Taozhi, and Central Palace Guard Commander Ku Di Shiwen racing to Jinyang, then led the army after them.

sentences.zh: 思好軍敗，與行思投水而死。

translations.literal: Sihao's army was defeated; he and Xingsi threw themselves into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Sihao's army was defeated; he and Xingsi drowned themselves.

sentences.zh: 其麾下二千人，桃枝圍之，且殺且招，終不降，以至於盡。

translations.literal: His two thousand followers were surrounded by Taozhi, who killed and summoned by turns; in the end none surrendered, and all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Taozhi surrounded his two thousand men, killing and summoning by turns; none would surrender, and all were slain.

sentences.zh: 時帝在道，叱奴世安自晉陽遂露布，于城平都遇斛斯孝卿，孝卿誘使食，因馳詣行宮，叫已了。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was on the road; Chinu Shi'an brought the victory bulletin from Jinyang; at Pingdu of Yucheng he met Hulü Xiaoqing, who enticed him to eat, then raced to the traveling palace and cried that all was finished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still on the road when Chinu Shi'an brought the victory bulletin from Jinyang; at Pingdu in Yucheng he met Hulü Xiaoqing, who persuaded him to eat, then raced to the traveling palace shouting that all was done.

sentences.zh: 帝大歡，左右呼萬歲。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; those about him shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed; his attendants shouted long life.

sentences.zh: 良久，世安乃以狀自陳。

translations.literal: After a long while Shi'an finally presented his own report.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long while did Shi'an present his own report.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「告爾何物事？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What affair did you report to him?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What business did you report to him?"

sentences.zh: 乃得坐食！

translations.literal: That you could sit down and eat!"
translations.idiomatic: And yet you sat down to eat!"

sentences.zh: 」於是賞孝卿而免世安罪。

translations.literal: He thereupon rewarded Xiaoqing and pardoned Shi'an's crime.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Xiaoqing and pardoned Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 暴思好屍七日，然後屠剝焚之，烹尚之於鄴市，令內參射其妃于宮內，仍火焚殺之。

translations.literal: Sihao's corpse was exposed for seven days, then butchered and burned; Shangzhi was boiled in the market at Ye; an inner attendant was ordered to shoot his consort within the palace, and she was then burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Sihao's corpse was exposed seven days, then butchered and burned; Shangzhi was boiled alive in the Ye market; a palace attendant shot his consort inside the palace, then burned her body.

sentences.zh: 思好反前五旬，有人告其謀反。

translations.literal: Fifty days before Sihao's rebellion someone reported that he was plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty days before the revolt someone reported Sihao's plot.

sentences.zh: 韓長鸞女適思好子，故奏言有人誣告諸貴，事相擾動，不殺無以息後，乃斬之。

translations.literal: Han Changluan's daughter was married to Sihao's son; he therefore memorialized that someone was falsely accusing the nobles and disturbing affairs, and that unless the informant was killed there would be no quieting the aftermath—so the man was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Han Changluan's daughter had married Sihao's son; he memorialized that nobles were being falsely accused and affairs disturbed, and that unless the informant was killed the trouble would not cease—so the man was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 思好既誅，死者弟伏闕下訴求贈兄，長鸞不為通也。

translations.literal: After Sihao was executed, the dead informant's younger brother knelt at the palace gate petitioning posthumous honors for his brother; Changluan would not pass the petition through.
translations.idiomatic: After Sihao's death the informant's younger brother petitioned at the gate for honors for his brother; Changluan refused to transmit it.

sentences.zh: 平秦王歸彥，字仁英，神武族弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, styled Renying, was Shenwu's clansman on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, styled Renying, was Gao Huan's paternal clansman.

sentences.zh: 父徽，魏末坐事當徙涼州。

translations.literal: His father Hui, at the end of Wei, was convicted of an offense and was to be banished to Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui, late in Wei, was convicted and sentenced to banishment in Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 行至河、渭間，遇賊，以軍功得免流。

translations.literal: Traveling between the He and Wei rivers he encountered bandits and, through military merit, was spared exile.
translations.idiomatic: Between the He and Wei rivers he met bandits and, through military merit, was spared exile.

sentences.zh: 因於河州積年，以解胡言為西域大使，得胡師子，以功行河東事，遂死焉。

translations.literal: He therefore remained many years in He Province; because he understood barbarian speech he became envoy to the Western Regions, obtained a barbarian lion, and through merit administered Hedong affairs, then died there.
translations.idiomatic: He remained many years in He Province; knowing barbarian languages he became envoy to the Western Regions, obtained a barbarian lion, and through merit administered Hedong, where he died.

sentences.zh: 徽于神武，舊恩甚篤。

translations.literal: Hui and Shenwu had an old bond of deep kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Gao Huan shared an old bond of deep kindness.

sentences.zh: 及神武平京洛，迎徽喪，與穆同營葬。

translations.literal: When Shenwu pacified Luoyang he welcomed Hui's coffin and buried him in the same camp as Mu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan took Luoyang he brought back Hui's coffin and buried him in the same camp as Mu.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister over the Masses with the posthumous title Wenhuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister over the Masses with the posthumous title Wenhuan.

sentences.zh: 濟南自晉陽之鄴，楊愔宣敕，留從駕兵五千於西中，陰備非常。

translations.literal: When Jinan went from Jinyang to Ye, Yang Yin proclaimed an edict leaving five thousand troops of the imperial escort in the Western Palace as a secret guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jinan went from Jinyang to Ye, Yang Yin proclaimed an edict leaving five thousand escort troops in the Western Palace as a secret precaution.

sentences.zh: 至鄴數日，歸彥乃知之，由是陰怨楊、燕等。

translations.literal: Several days after reaching Ye, Guiyan learned of it and therefore bore secret resentment toward Yang, Yan, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Several days after reaching Ye, Guiyan learned of it and secretly resented Yang, Yan, and their faction.

sentences.zh: 楊、燕等欲去二王，問計於歸彥。

translations.literal: Yang, Yan, and the others wished to remove the two princes and asked Guiyan's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, Yan, and their allies wished to remove the two princes and sought Guiyan's advice.

sentences.zh: 歸彥詐喜，請共元海量之。

translations.literal: Guiyan pretended delight and asked to deliberate together with Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan feigned delight and asked to consult Yuanhai together.

sentences.zh: 元海亦口許心違，馳告長廣。

translations.literal: Yuanhai also promised with his mouth while opposing in his heart, and raced to inform Prince Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai promised with his mouth but opposed in his heart, and raced to inform Prince Changguang.

sentences.zh: 長廣於是誅楊、燕等。

translations.literal: Prince Changguang thereupon executed Yang, Yan, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changguang thereupon executed Yang, Yan, and their allies.

sentences.zh: 孝昭將入雲龍門，都督成休甯列仗拒而不內，歸彥諭之，然後得入。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao was about to enter the Yunlong Gate, Commander Cheng Xiuning drew up troops and refused entry; Guiyan admonished him, and only then was entry granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao was about to enter Yunlong Gate, Commander Cheng Xiuning drew up troops and barred him; Guiyan persuaded him, and only then was entry granted.

sentences.zh: 進向柏閣、永巷亦知之。

translations.literal: Advancing toward the Cypress Pavilion and the Eternal Lane, he knew the way as well.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the way equally well advancing toward the Cypress Pavilion and the Eternal Lane.

sentences.zh: 孝昭踐阼，以此彌見優重。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao ascended the throne, for this he was all the more favored and honored.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao took the throne, Guiyan was all the more favored for this.

sentences.zh: 每入，常在平原王段韶上。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered court he was always placed above Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended court he was seated above Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao.

sentences.zh: 以為司空，兼尚書令。

translations.literal: He was made Minister of Works and concurrently Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Works and concurrently Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 齊制，宮內唯天子紗帽，臣下皆戎帽。

translations.literal: Under Qi regulations, within the palace only the Son of Heaven wore the gauze cap; all subjects wore military caps.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi law only the emperor wore the gauze cap within the palace; all officials wore military caps.

sentences.zh: 特賜歸彥紗帽以寵之。

translations.literal: Guiyan was specially granted a gauze cap as a mark of favor.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan alone was granted a gauze cap as a special mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 孝昭崩，歸彥從晉陽迎武成於鄴。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao died, Guiyan went from Jinyang to Ye to welcome Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao died, Guiyan went from Jinyang to Ye to welcome Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 及武成即位，進位太傅，領司徒，常聽將私部曲三人，帶刀入仗。

translations.literal: When Wucheng took the throne, Guiyan was advanced to Grand Tutor and headed the Secretariat, and was regularly permitted to bring three men of his private guard bearing swords into the guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng took the throne, Guiyan was made Grand Tutor and head of the Secretariat, and was regularly allowed three armed retainers from his private guard in the honor guard.

sentences.zh: 從武成還都，諸貴戚等競要之。

translations.literal: When he followed Wucheng back to the capital, the imperial kin and nobles all competed to entertain him.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital with Wucheng, the nobles all competed to host him.

sentences.zh: 其所往處，一坐盡傾。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, the whole company was won over.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went, the whole gathering was swayed.

sentences.zh: 歸彥既地居將相，志氣盈滿，發言陵侮，傍若無人。

translations.literal: Guiyan now stood at the rank of general and minister; his spirit was full to overflowing; in speech he was overbearing and insulting, as if no one were beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Now a general and minister, Guiyan's pride overflowed; he spoke with insulting arrogance as if no one else were present.

sentences.zh: 議者以威權震主，必為禍亂。

translations.literal: Commentators held that his authority shook the sovereign and would surely bring calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said his power overshadowed the throne and would surely bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 上亦尋其前翻覆之跡，漸忌之。

translations.literal: The sovereign also traced his earlier shifts of loyalty and gradually grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also recalled his earlier betrayals and grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 高元海、畢義雲、高乾和等咸數言其短。

translations.literal: Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, Gao Qianhe, and others repeatedly spoke of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, Gao Qianhe, and others repeatedly denounced him.

sentences.zh: 上幸歸彥家，召魏收對禦作詔草，欲加右丞相。

translations.literal: The sovereign visited Guiyan's home and summoned Wei Shou to draft an edict before the throne, intending to add the title of Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Guiyan's home and summoned Wei Shou to draft an edict in his presence, intending to make him Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 收曰：「至尊以右丞相登帝位，今為歸彥威名太盛，故出之，豈可復加此號？

translations.literal: Shou said, "His Majesty ascended the throne as Right Chancellor; now because Guiyan's fame and power are too great he is being sent out—how can this title be given again?"
translations.idiomatic: Shou said, "Your Majesty took the throne as Right Chancellor; now Guiyan's power is too great, so he is being sent away—how can that title be restored?"

sentences.zh: 」乃拜太宰、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was therefore appointed Grand Preceptor and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was instead appointed Grand Preceptor and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 即乾和繕寫。

translations.literal: Qianhe copied it out at once.
translations.idiomatic: Qianhe copied it out immediately.

sentences.zh: 晝日，仍敕門司不聽輒內。

translations.literal: In broad daylight an edict was still issued that the gate office was not to allow him to enter without permission.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict ordered the gate guards not to admit him without permission.

sentences.zh: 時歸彥在家縱酒，經宿不知，至明欲參。

translations.literal: At the time Guiyan was at home indulging in wine; he knew nothing all night; at dawn he wished to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan was at home drinking heavily and knew nothing until dawn, when he set out for court.

sentences.zh: 至門知之，大驚而退。

translations.literal: Reaching the gate he learned of it and withdrew in great alarm.
translations.idiomatic: At the gate he learned the news and fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 及通名謝，敕令早發，別賜錢帛、鼓吹、醫藥，事事周備。

translations.literal: When he announced himself to give thanks, an edict ordered him to set out early; he was separately granted money, silks, musicians, and medicines—everything was fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: When he presented thanks, an edict ordered him to depart early; money, silks, musicians, and medicines were all lavishly granted.

sentences.zh: 又敕武職督將，悉送至清陽宮。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered military supervisors and generals all to escort him to Qingyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Military supervisors and generals were ordered to escort him to Qingyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 拜而退，莫敢共語。

translations.literal: He bowed and withdrew; none dared speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed and withdrew; none dared speak with him.

sentences.zh: 唯與趙郡王睿久語，時無聞者。

translations.literal: Only with Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui did he speak at length; none overheard.
translations.idiomatic: Only with Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui did he speak at length; no one overheard.

sentences.zh: 至州不自安，謀逆，欲待受調訖，班賜軍士。

translations.literal: Reaching the province he was ill at ease and plotted rebellion, intending to wait until he had received his transfer orders and distributed rewards to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he grew uneasy and plotted rebellion, intending to wait until transfer orders came and he could reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 望車駕如晉陽，乘虛入鄴。

translations.literal: He hoped the imperial carriage would go to Jinyang so he could seize the chance to enter Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped the emperor would go to Jinyang so he could strike at Ye.

sentences.zh: 為其郎中令呂思禮所告，詔平原王段韶襲之。

translations.literal: His Bureau Director Lü Sil was informed and reported it; an edict ordered Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: His Bureau Director Lü Sil reported him; an edict ordered Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao to attack.

sentences.zh: 歸彥舊于南境置私驛，聞軍將逼，報之，便嬰城拒守。

translations.literal: Guiyan had long maintained private courier posts on the southern border; hearing that troops were pressing near, he sent word and at once closed the city and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan had long kept private courier posts on the southern border; hearing troops approach, he alerted his men and held the city.

sentences.zh: 先是，冀州長史宇文仲鸞、司馬李祖挹、別駕陳季璩、中從事房子弼、長樂郡守尉普興等疑歸彥有異，使連名密啟，歸彥追而獲之，遂收禁仲鸞等五人。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chief Administrator of Ji Province Yuwen Zhongluan, Vice Governor Li Zuyi, Vice Director Chen Jiji, Central Attendant Fang Zibi, and Administrator of Changle Commandery Wei Puxing and others suspected Guiyan of irregular intent and sent a joint secret memorial; Guiyan pursued and captured them, then imprisoned Zhongluan and the other five.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ji Province officials Yuwen Zhongluan, Li Zuyi, Chen Jiji, Fang Zibi, and Wei Puxing had suspected Guiyan and sent a joint secret memorial; he pursued them, seized them, and imprisoned all five.

sentences.zh: 仍並不從，皆殺之。

translations.literal: They still would not submit, and all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: They still refused submission, and all were killed.

sentences.zh: 軍已逼城，歸彥登城大叫云：「孝昭皇帝初崩，六軍百萬眾，悉由臣手，投身向鄴迎陛下。

translations.literal: The army had already pressed the city; Guiyan climbed the wall and shouted loudly, "When Emperor Xiaozhao first died, the six armies—a million men—were all in my hand; I threw myself into going to Ye to welcome Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: The army was at the walls; Guiyan climbed the ramparts and shouted, "When Emperor Xiaozhao died, a million men of the six armies were in my hands; I raced to Ye to welcome Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 當時不反，今日豈有異心？

translations.literal: I did not rebel then—how could I have a different intent today?"
translations.idiomatic: I did not rebel then—how could I rebel now?"

sentences.zh: 正恨高元海、畢義雲、高乾和誑惑聖上，疾忌忠良。

translations.literal: I truly hate only Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, and Gao Qianhe, who delude the sage sovereign and jealously harm the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: I hate only Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, and Gao Qianhe, who deceive the emperor and destroy the loyal.

sentences.zh: 但為殺此三人，即臨城自刎。

translations.literal: If only these three men are killed, I will come to the wall and cut my own throat."
translations.idiomatic: Kill these three and I will come to the wall and take my own life."

sentences.zh: 」其後城破，單騎北走。

translations.literal: Afterward the city fell; he fled north alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he fled north alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 至交津，見獲，鎖送鄴。

translations.literal: At Jiaojin he was captured and sent in chains to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiaojin he was captured and sent in chains to Ye.

sentences.zh: 帝令趙郡王睿私問其故，歸彥曰：「使黃頷少兒牽挽我，何可不反？

translations.literal: The emperor had Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui ask him privately the reason; Guiyan said, "To have yellow-bearded boys drag me about—how could I not rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui question him privately; Guiyan said, "When yellow-bearded boys drag me about, how could I not rebel?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「誰邪？

translations.literal: He was asked, "Who?"
translations.idiomatic: He was asked, "Who?"

sentences.zh: 」歸彥曰：「元海、乾和，豈是朝廷老宿？

translations.literal: Guiyan said, "Yuanhai and Qianhe—are they venerable elders of the court?"
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan said, "Yuanhai and Qianhe—are they the court's elder statesmen?"

sentences.zh: 如趙家老公時，又詎懷怨？

translations.literal: When it was like the old lord of the Zhao house, how could there be resentment?"
translations.idiomatic: When it was men like the old Zhao prince, how could I resent them?"

sentences.zh: 」於是帝又使讓焉。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon sent someone to reproach him again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent someone to reproach him again.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「高元海受畢義雲宅，用作本州刺史，給後部鼓吹，臣為蕃王、太宰，仍不得鼓吹。

translations.literal: He replied, "Gao Yuanhai took Bi Yiyun's residence for his own governorship and was given rear guard musicians; your servant was a frontier prince and Grand Preceptor yet still was not given musicians."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Gao Yuanhai took Bi Yiyun's house for his provincial seat and received imperial musicians; I was a frontier prince and Grand Preceptor yet got none."

sentences.zh: 正殺元海、義雲而已。

translations.literal: It is enough to kill Yuanhai and Yiyun."
translations.idiomatic: Killing Yuanhai and Yiyun would be enough."

sentences.zh: 」上令都督劉桃枝牽入，歸彥猶作前語，望活。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Commander Liu Taozhi to drag him in; Guiyan still spoke as before, hoping to live.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Commander Liu Taozhi to drag him in; Guiyan still repeated his plea, hoping to live.

sentences.zh: 帝命議其罪，皆云不可赦。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered deliberation on his crimes; all said he could not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his crimes debated; everyone agreed he could not be spared.

sentences.zh: 乃載以露車，銜枚面縛，劉桃枝臨之以刃，擊鼓隨之，並子孫十五人，皆棄市。

translations.literal: They then loaded him on an open cart, gagged and bound facing forward, with Liu Taozhi standing over him blade in hand and drums beating as they went; together with fifteen of his descendants, all were executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed on an open cart, gagged and bound face-forward, Liu Taozhi hovering over him with a blade while drums sounded; he and fifteen descendants were all put to death in the market.

sentences.zh: 贈仁州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Ren Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Governor of Ren Province.

sentences.zh: 魏時山崩，得石角二，藏在武庫。

translations.literal: During the Wei era a mountain collapsed and two stone horns were obtained; they were stored in the armory.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei times a landslide yielded two stone horns, which were kept in the imperial armory.

sentences.zh: 文宣入庫，賜從臣兵器，特以二石角與歸彥，謂曰：「爾事常山不得反，事長廣得反，反時，將此角嚇漢。

translations.literal: Wenxuan entered the armory, bestowed weapons upon his attending ministers, and specially gave the two stone horns to Guiyan, saying, "When you served the Prince of Changshan you could not rebel; when you served the Prince of Changguang you could rebel. When you rebel, use these horns to frighten the Han."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan entered the armory to distribute weapons among his followers and singled out the two stone horns for Guiyan, saying, "Serving the Prince of Changshan, you never rebelled; serving the Prince of Changguang, you did. When you rebel, scare the Han with these horns."

sentences.zh: 」歸彥額骨三道，著幘不安。

translations.literal: Guiyan had three ridges on his forehead; wearing a cap he was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan's forehead bore three prominent ridges, and a cap would not sit properly on his head.

sentences.zh: 文宣見之怒，使以馬鞭擊其額，血被面曰：「爾反時，當以此骨嚇漢。

translations.literal: Wenxuan saw this and grew angry; he had him struck on the forehead with a horsewhip until blood covered his face, saying, "When you rebel, you ought to use these bones to frighten the Han."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan flew into a rage at the sight and had his forehead lashed with a horsewhip until blood streamed down his face, saying, "When you rebel, frighten the Han with these bones of yours."

sentences.zh: 」其言反，竟驗云。

translations.literal: His words about rebellion were ultimately borne out.
translations.idiomatic: His talk of rebellion proved true in the end.

sentences.zh: 武興王普，字德廣，歸彥兄歸義之子也。

translations.literal: Prince Pu of Wuxing, styled Deguang, was the son of Guiyi, elder brother of Guiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pu of Wuxing, whose style name was Deguang, was the son of Guiyi, Guiyan's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 性寬和，有度量。

translations.literal: By nature he was mild and generous, possessed of breadth of character.
translations.idiomatic: He was mild and magnanimous by nature, with a generous temperament.

sentences.zh: 九歲歸彥自河州俱入洛，神武使與諸子同遊處。

translations.literal: At nine, when Guiyan came from He Province into Luoyang together with him, Gao Huan had him lodge and associate with his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: When he was nine, Guiyan brought him from He Province to Luoyang; Gao Huan had him live and study alongside his own sons.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封武興郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening years of Tianbao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuxing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 武平二年，累遷司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuping, through successive promotion he became Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuping he rose through successive posts to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 六年，為豫州道行台尚書令。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he became Chief of the Imperial Secretariat of the Mobile Headquarters for the Yuzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Chief of the Imperial Secretariat at the Yuzhou Circuit Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後主奔鄴，就加太宰。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord fled to Ye, he was additionally appointed Grand Mentor on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord fled to Ye, Pu was immediately given the additional title of Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 周師逼，乃降。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops pressed close, he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhou forces closed in, he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 卒于長安，贈上開府、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in Chang'an and was posthumously made Upper General Who Opens an Office and Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chang'an and was posthumously appointed Upper General Who Opens an Office and Governor of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 長樂太守靈山，字景嵩，神族族弟也。

translations.literal: Lingshan, Administrator of Changle, styled Jingsong, was a clansman of Gao Huan on the clan side.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshan, Administrator of Changle, styled Jingsong, was a clansman of Gao Huan's family.

sentences.zh: 從神武起兵信都，終長樂太守，贈大將軍、司空，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: He followed Gao Huan in raising troops at Xindu, ended as Administrator of Changle, was posthumously made Grand General and Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Wensuan.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Gao Huan's uprising at Xindu, served ultimately as Administrator of Changle, and was posthumously made Grand General and Minister of Works with the posthumous title Wensuan.

sentences.zh: 子懿，卒于武平鎮將。

translations.literal: His son Yi died as garrison commander of Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi died while serving as garrison commander of Wuping.

sentences.zh: 無子，文宣以靈山從父兄齊州刺史建國子伏護為靈山后。

translations.literal: Having no son, Wenxuan had Fuhu, son of Jianguo and Governor of Qi Province, who was Lingshan's father's elder brother's son, succeed Lingshan.
translations.idiomatic: With no heir of his own, Wenxuan appointed Fuhu—son of Jianguo, Governor of Qi Province and Lingshan's cousin on the father's side—as Lingshan's successor.

sentences.zh: 伏護字臣援，粗有刀筆。

translations.literal: Fuhu, styled Chenyuan, had a rough aptitude for writing and administration.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhu, styled Chenyuan, had a modest talent for letters and administration.

sentences.zh: 天統初，累遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiantong, through successive promotions he became Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tiantong era he rose through successive appointments to Attendant at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 伏護曆事數朝，恆參機要，而性嗜酒，每多醉失。

translations.literal: Fuhu served several reigns, constantly participating in confidential affairs, yet by nature he loved wine and often committed errors through drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhu served several emperors and was always involved in confidential matters, but he loved wine and frequently blundered while drunk.

sentences.zh: 末路逾劇，乃至連日不食，專事酣酒，神識恍惚，遂以卒。

translations.literal: In his last years it grew worse still, until for days on end he would not eat and devoted himself solely to heavy drinking; his spirit grew dim, and he thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years the habit worsened until he went days without eating and drank without cease; his mind clouded over, and he died.

sentences.zh: 贈袞州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 建國侯。

translations.literal: He was made Marquis of Jianguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianguo.

sentences.zh: 孫乂襲。

translations.literal: His grandson Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 乂少謹，武平末，給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Yi was careful from youth; at the end of Wuping he was Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was dutiful from youth; at the end of Wuping he served as Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中為太府少卿，坐事死。

translations.literal: Under Sui, in the Kaihuang era, he was Vice Director of the Palace Storehouse and was put to death for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui's Kaihuang era he served as Vice Director of the Palace Storehouse and was executed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 神武皇帝十五男：武明婁皇后生文襄皇帝、文宣皇帝、孝昭皇帝、襄城景王清、武成皇帝、博陵文簡王濟；

translations.literal: Gao Huan, Emperor Shenwu, had fifteen sons: Empress Wuming of the Lou clan bore Emperor Wenxiang, Emperor Wenxuan, Emperor Xiaozhao, Prince Qing of Xiangcheng Jing, Emperor Wucheng, and Prince Ji of Boling Wensuan;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenwu Gao Huan had fifteen sons. Empress Wuming of the Lou clan bore Emperor Wenxiang, Emperor Wenxuan, Emperor Xiaozhao, Prince Qing of Xiangcheng Jing, Emperor Wucheng, and Prince Ji of Boling Wensuan;

sentences.zh: 王氏生永安簡平王浚；

translations.literal: Lady Wang bore Prince Jun of Yong'an Jianping;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang bore Prince Jun of Yong'an Jianping;

sentences.zh: 穆氏生平陽靖翼王淹；

translations.literal: Lady Mu bore Prince Yan of Pingyang Jingyi;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mu bore Prince Yan of Pingyang Jingyi;

sentences.zh: 大爾硃氏生彭城景思王浟、華山王凝；

translations.literal: Lady Da Erzhu bore Prince You of Pengcheng Jingsi and Prince Ning of Huashan;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Da Erzhu bore Prince You of Pengcheng Jingsi and Prince Ning of Huashan;

sentences.zh: 韓氏生上党剛肅王渙；

translations.literal: Lady Han bore Prince Huan of Shangdang Gangsu;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Han bore Prince Huan of Shangdang Gangsu;

sentences.zh: 小爾硃氏生任城王湝；

translations.literal: Lady Xiao Erzhu bore Prince He of Rencheng;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiao Erzhu bore Prince He of Rencheng;

sentences.zh: 游氏生高陽康穆王氵是；

translations.literal: Lady You bore Prince Xie of Gaoyang Kangmu;
translations.idiomatic: Lady You bore Prince Xie of Gaoyang Kangmu;

sentences.zh: 鄭氏生馮翊王潤；

translations.literal: Lady Zheng bore Prince Run of Fengyi;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng bore Prince Run of Fengyi;

sentences.zh: 馬氏生漢陽敬懷王洽。

translations.literal: Lady Ma bore Prince Qia of Hanyang Jinghuai.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ma bore Prince Qia of Hanyang Jinghuai.

sentences.zh: 永安簡平王浚字定樂，神武第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Jun of Yong'an Jianping, styled Dingle, was Gao Huan's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun of Yong'an Jianping, whose style name was Dingle, was Gao Huan's third son.

sentences.zh: 初，神武納浚母，當月而有孕。

translations.literal: At first, when Gao Huan took Jun's mother, she became pregnant within the month.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan first took Jun's mother, she conceived within the same month.

sentences.zh: 及產浚，疑非己類，不甚愛之。

translations.literal: When Jun was born, he suspected the boy was not of his kind and did not love him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun was born, Gao Huan doubted the child was truly his and showed little affection.

sentences.zh: 而浚早慧，後更被寵。

translations.literal: Yet Jun was precocious from youth, and afterward came to be favored.
translations.idiomatic: But Jun proved precocious, and in time he won greater favor.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，謂博士盧裕曰：「祭神如神在，為有神邪？

translations.literal: At eight years he said to the Academician Lu Yu, "Sacrificing to the spirits as if they were present—does this mean there are spirits?
translations.idiomatic: At eight he asked the Academician Lu Yu, "When the text says 'sacrifice to the spirits as if they were present,' does that mean spirits exist?

sentences.zh: 無神邪？

translations.literal: Or no spirits?"
translations.idiomatic: Or that they do not?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「有。

translations.literal: The reply was, "There are."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu answered, "They exist."

sentences.zh: 」浚曰：「有神，當云祭神神在，何煩如字？

translations.literal: Jun said, "If there are spirits, one ought simply to say 'the spirit is present at the sacrifice'—why bother with the word 'as'?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "If spirits exist, one should say 'the spirit is present at the sacrifice.' Why add 'as if'?"

sentences.zh: 」景裕不能答。

translations.literal: Jingyu could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu had no reply.

sentences.zh: 及長，嬉戲不節。

translations.literal: When he grew up he played without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he indulged in unrestrained amusements.

sentences.zh: 曾以屬請受納，大見杖罰，拘禁府獄，既而見原。

translations.literal: Once for accepting bribes through petitioners he was severely beaten with the staff, imprisoned in the princely gaol, then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was caught taking bribes through intermediaries, severely flogged, and confined in the princely prison before being pardoned.

sentences.zh: 後稍折節，頗以讀書為務。

translations.literal: Later he somewhat reformed himself and took reading as his chief occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Later he checked his ways somewhat and devoted himself to study.

sentences.zh: 元象中，封永安郡公。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yong'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yong'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 豪爽有氣力，善騎射，為文襄所愛。

translations.literal: Bold and generous, possessed of strength, skilled in riding and archery—he was loved by Prince Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and vigorous, skilled at riding and archery, and was beloved by Prince Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 文宣性雌懦，每參文襄，有時洟出。

translations.literal: Wenxuan was timid by nature; whenever he attended upon Prince Wenxiang his nose would sometimes run.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan was timid by nature; whenever he attended Prince Wenxiang his nose would sometimes drip.

sentences.zh: 浚恆責帝左右：「何因不為二兄拭鼻？

translations.literal: Jun constantly rebuked the emperor's attendants: "Why do you not wipe Second Brother's nose?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun would scold the emperor's attendants: "Why don't you wipe Second Brother's nose for him?"

sentences.zh: 」由是見銜。

translations.literal: Because of this Wenxuan came to bear a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan took deep offense at this.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書監、兼侍中。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and concurrent Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 出為青州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 雖頗好畋獵，聰明矜恕，上下畏悅之。

translations.literal: Although he was quite fond of hunting, he was intelligent, self-restrained and forgiving; superiors and subordinates both feared and delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: Though fond of the hunt, he was clever, self-controlled, and merciful; men above and below him both respected and admired him.

sentences.zh: 保定初，進爵為王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding his rank was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Baoding his title was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 文宣末年多酒，浚謂親近曰：「二兄舊來，不甚了了，自登阼已後，識解頓進。

translations.literal: In Wenxuan's last years he drank heavily; Jun said to those close to him, "Second Brother was formerly not very clear-minded; since ascending the throne his understanding has suddenly advanced.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenxuan's later years he drank heavily. Jun told his intimates, "Second Brother was never very sharp, but since taking the throne his judgment has improved dramatically.

sentences.zh: 今因酒敗德，朝臣無敢諫者。

translations.literal: Now through wine he is ruining his virtue, and no court official dares remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Now wine is destroying his character, and not one court official dares speak up.

sentences.zh: 大敵未滅，吾甚以為憂。

translations.literal: The great enemy is not yet destroyed—I am deeply troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Our great enemy is still undefeated, and I am deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 欲乘驛至鄴面諫，不知用吾不？

translations.literal: I wish to ride the courier post to Ye and remonstrate face to face—will my counsel be heeded?"
translations.idiomatic: I want to take the post road to Ye and remonstrate with him in person. Will he listen to me?"

sentences.zh: 」人有知，密以白帝，又見銜。

translations.literal: Someone heard of it and secretly reported to the emperor; again Wenxuan bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Someone overheard and secretly informed the emperor, who nursed another grievance against him.

sentences.zh: 八年，來朝，從幸東山。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he came to court and accompanied the emperor to Mount Dong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he came to court and joined the emperor on an excursion to Mount Dong.

sentences.zh: 帝裸裎為樂，雜以婦女，又作狐掉尾戲。

translations.literal: The emperor disported himself naked for amusement, mingling with women, and also performed the "fox wagging tail" play.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor amused himself naked among the women and staged the "fox wagging its tail" game.

sentences.zh: 浚進言，此非人主所宜。

translations.literal: Jun advanced remonstrance: this was not fitting for a sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Jun spoke up that such conduct was unbecoming of a ruler.

sentences.zh: 帝甚不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 浚又于屏處召楊遵彥，譏其不諫。

translations.literal: Jun also summoned Yang Zunyan aside and reproached him for not remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: Jun also pulled Yang Zunyan aside and rebuked him for failing to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 帝時不欲大臣與諸王交通，遵彥懼，以奏帝。

translations.literal: The emperor at the time did not wish great ministers to associate with princes; Zunyan grew afraid and reported it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had forbidden senior ministers from consorting with princes; Zunyan, alarmed, reported the conversation.

sentences.zh: 大怒曰：「小人由來難忍！

translations.literal: He flew into a rage and said, "This petty fellow has always been hard to tolerate!"
translations.idiomatic: He exploded in anger: "That wretch has always been unbearable!"

sentences.zh: 」遂罷酒還宮。

translations.literal: He thereupon ended the feast and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He broke off the revelry at once and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 浚尋還州，又上書切諫。

translations.literal: Before long Jun returned to his province and again submitted a memorial of forceful remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after returning to his province, Jun sent another memorial of blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 詔令徵浚，浚懼禍，謝疾不朝。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jun summoned; fearing disaster, he pleaded illness and did not come to court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Jun to court; fearing punishment, he pleaded illness and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 上怒，馳驛收浚，老幼泣送者數千人。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and sent courier riders to seize Jun; old and young, weeping as they saw him off, numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent fast riders to arrest him; thousands of old and young wept as they watched him go.

sentences.zh: 至，盛以鐵籠，與上党王渙俱置北城地牢下，飲食溲穢，共在一所。

translations.literal: When he arrived, they confined him in an iron cage and placed him together with Prince Huan of Shangdang in an underground dungeon beneath the north city; food and filth shared the same space.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was shut in an iron cage and thrown into an underground pit beneath the north city together with Prince Huan of Shangdang, where they ate and relieved themselves in the same confined space.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝親將左右，臨穴歌謳，令浚等和之。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor personally led his attendants, came to the pit, and sang; he ordered Jun and the others to join in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor brought his attendants to the pit, sang songs himself, and ordered Jun and the others to join in.

sentences.zh: 浚等惶怖且悲，不覺聲戰。

translations.literal: Jun and the others were fearful and sorrowful; without knowing it their voices trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and the others, terrified and grief-stricken, could not keep their voices steady.

sentences.zh: 帝為愴然，因泣，將赦之。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to pity, wept, and was about to pardon them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was touched, wept, and was on the verge of granting a pardon.

sentences.zh: 長廣王湛先與浚不睦，進曰：「猛獸安可出穴？

translations.literal: Prince Zhan of Changguang, who had long been on bad terms with Jun, advanced and said, "How can a fierce beast be let out of its den?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhan of Changguang, who had long been at odds with Jun, stepped forward and said, "You cannot let a savage beast out of its lair."

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 浚等聞之，呼長廣王小字曰：「步落稽，皇天見汝！

translations.literal: Jun and the others, hearing this, cried out Prince Changguang's childhood name: "Buluoqi—Heaven sees you!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Jun and the others shouted Prince Changguang's childhood name: "Buluoqi—Heaven is watching you!"

sentences.zh: 」左右聞者，莫不悲傷。

translations.literal: Those among the attendants who heard were all grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Every attendant who heard was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 浚與渙皆有雄略，為諸王所傾服。

translations.literal: Jun and Huan both possessed bold strategy and were admired by all the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Huan were both men of bold counsel, and the other princes looked up to them.

sentences.zh: 帝恐為害，乃自刺渙，又使壯士劉桃枝就籠亂刺。

translations.literal: The emperor feared they would cause harm; he personally stabbed Huan, then sent the strong man Liu Taozhi to stab wildly at the cage.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing they would prove dangerous, the emperor stabbed Huan himself, then sent the strongman Liu Taozhi to thrust wildly into the cage.

sentences.zh: 槊每下，浚、渙輒以手拉折之，號哭呼天，於是薪火亂投籠，燒殺之，填以石土。

translations.literal: With each thrust of the spear, Jun and Huan would grab and break it, wailing and calling to Heaven; then firewood was thrown pell-mell into the cage and they were burned to death, and the pit was filled with stone and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Each time a spear thrust down, Jun and Huan grabbed and snapped it, wailing to Heaven; then firewood was heaped into the cage and they were burned alive, and the pit was filled with stone and earth.

sentences.zh: 後出，皮發皆盡，屍色如炭，天下為之痛心。

translations.literal: When they were later exhumed, skin and hair were entirely gone and the corpses were charcoal-black; all under Heaven grieved for them.
translations.idiomatic: When the bodies were later dug up, skin and hair had burned away and the corpses were black as charcoal; the whole realm mourned them.

sentences.zh: 後帝以其妃陸氏配儀同劉鬱捷，舊帝蒼頭也，以軍功見寵。

translations.literal: Later the emperor gave Jun's consort, the Lady Lu, to Yitong Liu Yujie—a former palace menial of the emperor who had won favor through military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor gave Jun's consort, Lady Lu, to Liu Yujie, a Yitong who had once been the emperor's personal servant and risen through military merit.

sentences.zh: 時令鬱捷害浚，故以配焉。

translations.literal: At the time he had ordered Yujie to kill Jun, and therefore gave her to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier ordered Yujie to kill Jun, and so gave her to him as a wife.

sentences.zh: 後數日，帝以陸氏先無寵於浚，敕與離絕。

translations.literal: Several days later the emperor, on the grounds that Lady Lu had formerly received no favor from Jun, ordered them separated.
translations.idiomatic: Days later, citing the fact that Lady Lu had never been favored by Jun, the emperor ordered them parted.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ganming he was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ganming he was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 無子，詔以彭城王浟第二子准字茂則嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, an edict had Zhun, styled Maoze, second son of Prince You of Pengcheng, succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: With no heir of his own, an edict named Zhun, styled Maoze, second son of Prince You of Pengcheng, as his successor.

sentences.zh: 彭城景思王浟，字子深，神武第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince You of Pengcheng Jingsi, styled Zishen, was Gao Huan's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince You of Pengcheng Jingsi, whose style name was Zishen, was Gao Huan's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 元象二年，拜通直散騎常侍，封長樂郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanxiang he was appointed Regular Attendant on Fast Direct Access and enfeoffed as Duke of Changle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanxiang he was made Regular Attendant on Fast Direct Access and enfeoffed as Duke of Changle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 博士韓毅教浟書，見浟筆跡未工，戲浟曰：「五郎書畫如此，忽為常侍開國，今日後，宜更用心！

translations.literal: The Academician Han Yi taught You writing; seeing You's handwriting was not yet skilled, he joked, "Fifth Son, with writing and drawing like this, yet suddenly made a Regular Attendant and enfeoffed—hereafter you ought to apply yourself more diligently!"
translations.idiomatic: The Academician Han Yi tutored You in writing; seeing his penmanship was still poor, he teased him, "Fifth Son, with handwriting like this—and yet you've become a Regular Attendant and received a fief! From now on you'd better work harder!"

sentences.zh: 」浟正色答曰：「昔甘羅為秦相，未聞能書。

translations.literal: You answered gravely, "In former times Gan Luo became Chancellor of Qin—one never heard that he could write.
translations.idiomatic: You replied sternly, "Gan Luo became Chancellor of Qin at a young age, and no one ever praised his calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 凡人唯論才具何如，豈必勤勤筆跡。

translations.literal: For ordinary men it is only talent and capacity that matter—why must one toil over penmanship?"
translations.idiomatic: What matters in a man is talent and ability—why must one slave over pen strokes?"

sentences.zh: 博士當今能者，何為不作三公？

translations.literal: If the Academician is so capable today, why are you not one of the Three Dukes?"
translations.idiomatic: If you are so accomplished, Academician, why aren't you one of the Three Dukes?"

sentences.zh: 」時年蓋八歲矣。

translations.literal: He was then about eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was then about eight years old.

sentences.zh: 毅甚慚。

translations.literal: Yi felt deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 武定六年，出為滄州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wuding, he was sent out to serve as Governor of Cang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wuding, he was posted as Governor of Cang Province.

sentences.zh: 為政嚴察，部內肅然。

translations.literal: His governance was strict and exacting; within his jurisdiction all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with strict scrutiny, and his domain was thoroughly subdued.

sentences.zh: 守令參佐，下及胥吏，行遊往來，皆自齎糧食。

translations.literal: From prefects and magistrates to their aides, down to clerks and runners, all traveling on official business had to carry their own provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects, magistrates, and their aides, down to the clerks and runners—everyone traveling on official business had to carry his own food.

sentences.zh: 浟纖介知人間事，有隰沃縣主簿張達，嘗詣州，夜投人舍，食雞羹，浟察知之。

translations.literal: You knew human affairs down to the smallest detail. Zhang Da, chief secretary of Xiwo County, once came to the provincial capital; one night he lodged at someone's home and ate chicken soup, and You detected it through his scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: You knew the smallest details of human affairs. Zhang Da, chief secretary of Xiwo County, once visited the capital; one night he lodged at a private house and ate chicken soup, and You found out.

sentences.zh: 守令畢集，浟對眾曰：「食雞羹何不還他價直也？

translations.literal: When the prefects and magistrates were all assembled, You said before the gathering, "After eating chicken soup, why not pay the owner his price?
translations.idiomatic: When the prefects and magistrates had all gathered, You said before them all, "You ate chicken soup—why not pay the owner what you owe?"

sentences.zh: 」達即伏罪，合境號為神明。

translations.literal: Zhang Da immediately confessed his guilt, and the entire jurisdiction hailed You as divine in his judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Da immediately confessed, and the whole region proclaimed You a divine judge.

sentences.zh: 又有一人從幽州來，驢馱鹿脯。

translations.literal: Another man came from You Province, his donkey loaded with dried venison.
translations.idiomatic: Another man came from You Province with a donkey carrying dried venison.

sentences.zh: 至滄州界，腳痛行遲，偶會一人為伴，遂盜驢及脯去。

translations.literal: Reaching the borders of Cang Province, his foot pained him and he walked slowly; he chanced to meet a companion, who then stole the donkey and the venison and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the border of Cang Province, his foot hurt and he walked slowly; he happened to meet a traveling companion, who then stole his donkey and venison and fled.

sentences.zh: 明旦告州，浟乃令左右及府僚吏分市鹿膊，不限其價。

translations.literal: At dawn he reported to the province; You then ordered his attendants and the staff of the prefectural office to go separately and buy venison shoulder, without limiting the price.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he reported to the provincial office; You then ordered his attendants and the staff of the prefectural office to go out separately and buy venison shoulder, with no limit on price.

sentences.zh: 其主見脯識之，推獲盜者。

translations.literal: The owner saw the venison and recognized it; tracking from there, they captured the thief.
translations.idiomatic: The owner saw the venison and recognized it; following the lead, they captured the thief.

sentences.zh: 轉都督、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as Area Commander and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Area Commander and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 時有人被盜黑牛，背上有白毛。

translations.literal: At the time someone had a black ox stolen from him; it had white hair on its back.
translations.idiomatic: At the time someone had a black ox stolen; it had white hair on its back.

sentences.zh: 長史韋道建謂中從事魏道勝曰：「使君在滄州日，禽奸如神。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Wei Daojian said to Senior Aide Wei Daosheng, "When our lord served in Cang Province, he seized wrongdoers as though by divine aid.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Wei Daojian said to Senior Aide Wei Daosheng, "When our lord was in Cang Province, he caught criminals as if by divine power.

sentences.zh: 若捉得此賊，定神矣。

translations.literal: If he catches this thief too, he will surely prove divine once more.
translations.idiomatic: If he catches this thief, he will surely prove divine again."

sentences.zh: 」浟乃詐為上符，市牛皮，倍酬價直。

translations.literal: You then forged an upper directive and had ox hides purchased at double the market price.
translations.idiomatic: You then forged an imperial directive and had ox hides purchased at double the market price.

sentences.zh: 使牛主認之，因獲其盜。

translations.literal: He had the ox's owner identify it, and thus captured the thief.
translations.idiomatic: He had the ox's owner identify it, and thus captured the thief.

sentences.zh: 建等嘆服。

translations.literal: Wei Daojian and the others sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Daojian and the others sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 又有老母姓王，孤獨，種菜三畝，數被偷。

translations.literal: There was also an old woman surnamed Wang, living alone, who planted vegetables on three mu of land and suffered repeated thefts.
translations.idiomatic: There was also an old woman surnamed Wang, living alone, who planted vegetables on three mu of land and was robbed again and again.

sentences.zh: 浟乃令人密往書菜葉為字，明日，市中看菜葉有字，獲賊。

translations.literal: You then secretly had someone inscribe characters on the vegetable leaves; the next day, examining the leaves in the market, they found the characters and captured the thief.
translations.idiomatic: You secretly had someone inscribe characters on the vegetable leaves; the next day, when the leaves with writing appeared in the market, they captured the thief.

sentences.zh: 爾後境內無盜，政化為當時第一。

translations.literal: After that there were no thieves within the borders; his governance ranked first among his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: After that there were no thieves in the region, and his governance was ranked first in the age.

sentences.zh: 浟明練世務，果於斷決，事無大小，咸悉以情。

translations.literal: You was thoroughly versed in worldly affairs, decisive in judgment; matters great and small were all handled according to their true circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: You was thoroughly versed in affairs of state, resolute in judgment; matters great and small were all decided according to the facts.

sentences.zh: 趙郡李公統預高歸彥之逆，其母崔氏，即御史中丞崔昂從父姊，兼右僕射魏收之內妹也。

translations.literal: Li Gongtong of Zhao Commandery was implicated in Gao Guiyan's rebellion; his mother Lady Cui was Elder Censor-in-Chief Cui Ang's father's cousin on his father's side, and also Right Vice Director Wei Shou's wife's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongtong of Zhao Commandery was implicated in Gao Guiyan's rebellion; his mother Lady Cui was the paternal cousin of Elder Censor-in-Chief Cui Ang and also the younger sister of Right Vice Director Wei Shou's wife.

sentences.zh: 依令，年出六十，例免入官。

translations.literal: According to the statute, anyone over sixty was by rule exempt from being taken into official custody.
translations.idiomatic: According to the law, anyone over sixty was by precedent exempt from being seized for official punishment.

sentences.zh: 崔增年陳訴，所司以昂、收故，崔遂獲免。

translations.literal: Lady Cui falsely claimed to be older to plead exemption; the responsible office, out of regard for Cui Ang and Wei Shou, let Lady Cui go free.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui falsely added years to her age in her petition; the responsible office, out of regard for Cui Ang and Wei Shou, granted her exemption.

sentences.zh: 浟摘發其事，昂等以罪除名。

translations.literal: You exposed the matter; Cui Ang and the others were stripped of their names and offices for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: You exposed the affair, and Cui Ang and the others were dismissed and stripped of their names for their offense.

sentences.zh: 自後車駕巡幸，浟常留鄴。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever the imperial carriage went on tour, You was regularly left behind at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever the emperor went on tour, You was regularly left behind at Ye.

sentences.zh: 河清三年三月，群盜白子禮等數十人，謀劫浟為主。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Heqing, a band of dozens led by the outlaw Bai Zili plotted to seize You and make him their leader.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Heqing, a band of dozens led by the outlaw Bai Zili plotted to seize You and make him their chief.

sentences.zh: 詐稱使者，徑向浟第。

translations.literal: They feigned to be imperial envoys and went straight to You's residence.
translations.idiomatic: They pretended to be imperial envoys and went straight to You's residence.

sentences.zh: 至內室，稱敕呼浟，牽上馬，臨以白刃，欲引向南殿。

translations.literal: Reaching the inner chambers, they claimed an edict and summoned You, dragged him onto a horse, threatened him with naked blades, and sought to lead him toward the Southern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the inner chambers, they claimed an edict and summoned You, dragged him onto a horse, held naked blades to his throat, and tried to lead him toward the Southern Hall.

sentences.zh: 浟大呼不從，遂遇害，時年三十二。

translations.literal: You cried out and refused to obey; he was thereupon murdered, aged thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: You cried out and refused to obey; he was thereupon killed, at the age of thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 朝野痛惜焉。

translations.literal: The court and the people mourned him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The court and the common people mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 初浟未被劫前，其妃鄭氏夢人斬浟頭持去，惡之。

translations.literal: Before You was seized, his consort Lady Zheng dreamed that someone cut off You's head and carried it away—a dream she found ominous.
translations.idiomatic: Before You was seized, his consort Lady Zheng dreamed that someone cut off You's head and carried it away; she took it as an evil omen.

sentences.zh: 數日而浟見殺。

translations.literal: Within days You was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Within days You was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、太師、太尉、錄尚書事，給轀輬車。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and furnished with an imperial funeral carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, along with an imperial funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 子寶德嗣。

translations.literal: His son Bao De succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bao De succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 位開府，兼尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He reached the rank of Commissioner with an Open Office and concurrently served as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Commissioner with an Open Office and concurrently served as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 上党剛肅王渙，字敬壽，神武第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince Gangsu of Shangdang, Huan, styled Jingshou, was the seventh son of Shenwu.
