translations.idiomatic: Prince Gangsu of Shangdang, Huan, whose style name was Jingshou, was the seventh son of Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 天姿雄傑，俶儻不群。

translations.literal: By nature he was heroic and outstanding, bold and unlike ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was heroic and outstanding, bold and unlike the common run of men.

sentences.zh: 雖在童幼，恆以將略自許。

translations.literal: Even as a child, he constantly prided himself on his generalship.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child, he constantly prided himself on his military talent.

sentences.zh: 神武壯而愛之，曰：「此兒似我。

translations.literal: Shenwu admired him and loved him, saying, "This boy is like me.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu admired him and loved him, saying, "This boy is like me."

sentences.zh: 」及長，力能扛鼎，材武絕倫。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his strength could lift a cauldron; in talent and martial prowess he had no peer.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he had the strength to lift a cauldron; in talent and martial prowess he had no equal.

sentences.zh: 每謂左右曰：「人不可無學，但要不為博士耳。

translations.literal: He often told his attendants, "A man must not be without learning—only he need not become a textual scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He often told his attendants, "A man must not be without learning—he need only avoid becoming a pedantic scholar."

sentences.zh: 」故讀書頗知梗概，而不甚耽習。

translations.literal: Thus he read books and gained a fair grasp of essentials, but did not devote himself deeply to study.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he read books and grasped the main points, but did not devote himself deeply to study.

sentences.zh: 元象中，封平原郡公。

translations.literal: During the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 文襄之遇賊，渙年尚幼，在西學。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang fell to assassins, Huan was still young, studying in the Western Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang was killed by assassins, Huan was still young and studying in the Western Academy.

sentences.zh: 聞宮中訁雚，驚曰：「大兄必遭難矣！

translations.literal: Hearing uproar in the palace, he exclaimed in alarm, "The eldest brother must have met disaster!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing uproar in the palace, he cried out in alarm, "The eldest brother must have met disaster!"

sentences.zh: 」彎弓而出。

translations.literal: He strung his bow and rushed out.
translations.idiomatic: He strung his bow and rushed out.

sentences.zh: 武定末，除冀州刺史，在州有美政。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was appointed Governor of Ji Province, where he governed admirably.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was appointed Governor of Ji Province, where his governance won praise.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封上党王，曆中書令、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shangdang, and successively served as Director of the Palace Secretariat and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shangdang, and successively served as Director of the Palace Secretariat and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 與常山王演等築伐惡諸城。

translations.literal: Together with Prince of Changshan Yan and others, he built the fortress-cities of the Fae campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Prince of Changshan Yan and others, he built the Fae fortresses.

sentences.zh: 遂聚鄴下輕薄，陵犯郡縣，為法司所糾。

translations.literal: He then gathered the riffraff of Ye, harassing and violating prefectures and counties, and was impeached by the judiciary.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered the idle and dissolute of Ye, harassing prefectures and counties, and was impeached by the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 文宣戮其左右數人，渙亦被譴。

translations.literal: Wenxuan executed several of his attendants, and Huan himself was censured.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan executed several of his attendants, and Huan himself was reprimanded.

sentences.zh: 六年，率眾送梁王蕭明還江南，仍破東關，斬梁特進裴之橫等，威名甚盛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he led troops escorting Prince Xiao Ming of Liang back to the Jiangnan, then broke through Dongguan Pass and slew Liang's Special Advance Pei Zhiheng and others; his martial renown grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he led troops escorting Prince Xiao Ming of Liang back to the Jiangnan, then broke through Dongguan Pass and slew Liang's Special Advance Pei Zhiheng and others; his martial fame grew greatly.

sentences.zh: 八年，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 初，術士言亡高者黑衣，由是自神武后每出行不欲見桑門，為黑衣故也。

translations.literal: Earlier, a diviner had said that the Gao who would perish would wear black; for this reason, from Shenwu's time onward, whenever they traveled abroad they did not wish to encounter Buddhist monks, because monks wore black.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a diviner had said that the Gao who would perish would wear black; for this reason, from Shenwu's time onward, whenever the family traveled abroad they did not wish to encounter Buddhist monks, because monks wore black.

sentences.zh: 是時文宣幸晉陽，以所忌問左右曰：「何物最黑？

translations.literal: At this time Wenxuan was visiting Jinyang and, brooding on what he feared, asked his attendants, "What thing is blackest?
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wenxuan was visiting Jinyang and, brooding on what he feared, asked his attendants, "What thing is blackest?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「莫過漆。

translations.literal: They answered, "Nothing blacker than lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Nothing blacker than lacquer."

sentences.zh: 」帝以渙第七，為當之，乃使庫真都督破六韓伯升之鄴徵渙。

translations.literal: The emperor, thinking Huan was seventh in birth and therefore the one foretold, sent Kuguan Commander Poluohan Bosheng to Ye to summon Huan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, thinking Huan was seventh in birth and therefore the one foretold, sent Kuguan Commander Poluohan Bosheng to Ye to summon Huan.

sentences.zh: 渙至紫陌橋，殺伯升以逃，憑河而度，土人執以送帝。

translations.literal: Huan reached Zimo Bridge, killed Bosheng to escape, and forded the river; local men seized him and delivered him to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Huan reached Zimo Bridge, killed Bosheng to escape, and forded the river; local men seized him and delivered him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 鐵籠盛之，與永安王浚同置地牢下。

translations.literal: He was confined in an iron cage and placed together with Prince Yong'an Jun in an underground dungeon.
translations.idiomatic: He was confined in an iron cage and placed together with Prince Yong'an Jun in an underground dungeon.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，與浚同見殺，時年二十六。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was executed together with Jun, aged twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was executed together with Jun, at the age of twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 以其妃李氏配馮文洛，是帝家舊奴，積勞位至刺史。

translations.literal: His consort Lady Li was given in marriage to Feng Wenluo, a former household slave of the imperial family who through accumulated service had risen to the governorship of a province.
translations.idiomatic: His consort Lady Li was given in marriage to Feng Wenluo, a former household slave of the imperial family who through long service had risen to provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 帝令文洛等殺渙，故以其妻妻焉。

translations.literal: The emperor had Feng Wenluo and the others kill Huan, and therefore gave him Huan's wife as his own.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Feng Wenluo and the others kill Huan, and therefore gave him Huan's wife as his own.

sentences.zh: 至乾明元年，收二王餘骨葬之，贈司空，諡曰剛肅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ganming the leftover bones of the two princes were gathered and buried; Huan was posthumously given the rank of Minister of Works and the temple name Gangsu ("Resolute and Stern").
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ganming the remaining bones of the two princes were gathered and buried; Huan was posthumously given Minister of Works and the posthumous title Gangsu, "Resolute and Stern."

sentences.zh: 有敕李氏還第，而文洛尚以故意，修飾詣李。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lady Li to return to her own residence, but Feng Wenluo, still clinging to their old arrangement, made himself fine and went to visit Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Lady Li to return to her own residence, but Feng Wenluo, still acting on their old relationship, dressed himself up and went to visit Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 李盛列左右，引文洛立於階下，數之曰「遭難流離，以至大辱，志操寡薄，不能自盡。

translations.literal: Lady Li arrayed her attendants in full and had Feng Wenluo brought to stand below the steps; she upbraided him, saying, "I met disaster and was cast into exile, coming to this great humiliation; my resolve is faint and I could not end my own life.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li arrayed her attendants in full and had Feng Wenluo brought to stand below the steps; she upbraided him, saying, "I met disaster and was cast into exile, coming to this great humiliation; my resolve was too weak and I could not end my own life.

sentences.zh: 幸蒙恩詔，得反籓闈。

translations.literal: By good fortune I received a gracious edict and was allowed to return to my princely household.
translations.idiomatic: By good fortune I received an imperial edict and was allowed to return to my princely household."

sentences.zh: 汝是誰家孰奴？

translations.literal: What family's low slave are you,
translations.idiomatic: What family's lowborn slave are you,

sentences.zh: 猶欲見侮！

translations.literal: yet you still wish to insult me!
translations.idiomatic: yet you still wish to insult me!"

sentences.zh: 」於是杖之一百，流血灑地。

translations.literal: She then had him beaten one hundred strokes until blood spread across the ground.
translations.idiomatic: She then had him beaten one hundred strokes until blood spread across the ground.

sentences.zh: 渙無嫡子，庶長子寶嚴，以河清二年襲爵。

translations.literal: Huan had no legitimate son; his eldest born son Bao Yan succeeded to the title in the second year of Heqing.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had no legitimate son; his eldest born son Bao Yan succeeded to the title in the second year of Heqing.

sentences.zh: 位終金紫光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He ultimately held the posts of Grand Master of Golden Letters and Purple Radiance and Commissioner with the privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He ultimately held the posts of Grand Master of Golden Letters and Purple Radiance and Commissioner with the privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 亮字彥道，性恭孝，美風儀，好文學。

translations.literal: Liang, styled Yandao, was by nature respectful and filial, with a fine bearing, and loved literature.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, whose style name was Yandao, was by nature respectful and filial, with a fine bearing, and loved literature.

sentences.zh: 為徐州刺史，坐奪商人財物，免官。

translations.literal: As Governor of Xu Province he was dismissed from office for seizing merchants' property.
translations.idiomatic: As Governor of Xu Province he was dismissed from office for seizing merchants' property.

sentences.zh: 後主敗，奔鄴，亮從焉。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord was defeated and fled to Ye, Liang followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord was defeated and fled to Ye, Liang followed him.

sentences.zh: 遷兼太尉、太傅。

translations.literal: He was promoted to serve concurrently as Grand Commandant and Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to serve concurrently as Grand Commandant and Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 周師入鄴，亮于啟夏門拒守，諸軍皆不戰而敗，周軍于諸城門皆入，亮軍方退走。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops entered Ye, Liang defended at Qixia Gate; the other armies all collapsed without fighting, Zhou forces entered through every city gate, and only then did Liang's army retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou troops entered Ye, Liang defended at Qixia Gate; the other armies all collapsed without fighting, Zhou forces entered through every city gate, and only then did Liang's army withdraw.

sentences.zh: 亮入太廟行馬內，慟哭拜辭，然後為周軍所執。

translations.literal: Liang entered the Imperial Temple within the Horse Gallop precinct, wept bitterly in farewell obeisance, and only then was seized by Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liang entered the Imperial Temple within the Horse Gallop precinct, wept bitterly in farewell obeisance, and only then was seized by Zhou troops.

sentences.zh: 入關，依例授儀同，分配遠邊，卒于龍州。

translations.literal: After entering the pass he was granted Yitong by custom, assigned to the far frontier, and died at Long Province.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the pass he was granted Yitong by custom, assigned to the far frontier, and died at Long Province.

sentences.zh: 時有婦人臨汾水浣衣，有乘馬人換其新靴馳而去者。

translations.literal: At the time a woman was washing clothes beside the Fen River when a man on horseback swapped her new boots for his old ones and galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a woman was washing clothes beside the Fen River when a man on horseback swapped her new boots for his old ones and galloped away.

sentences.zh: 婦人持故靴詣州言之。

translations.literal: The woman took the old boots and reported the matter at the provincial office.
translations.idiomatic: The woman took the old boots and reported the matter at the provincial office.

sentences.zh: 湝召居城諸嫗，以靴示之，紿曰：「有乘馬人于路被賊劫害，遺此靴，焉得無親屬乎？

translations.literal: Tang summoned all the old women living in the city and showed them the boots, falsely saying, "A man on horseback was robbed and killed on the road; he left these boots behind—surely he must have relatives among you?
translations.idiomatic: Tang summoned all the old women living in the city and showed them the boots, falsely saying, "A man on horseback was robbed and killed on the road; he left these boots behind—surely he must have relatives among you?"

sentences.zh: 」一嫗撫膺哭曰：「兒昨著此靴向妻家。

translations.literal: One old woman beat her breast and wept, saying, "My son wore these boots yesterday when he went to his wife's family.
translations.idiomatic: One old woman beat her breast and wept, saying, "My son wore these boots yesterday when he went to his wife's family."

sentences.zh: 」如其語，捕獲之，時稱明察。

translations.literal: Following her words, they captured the culprit; at the time he was praised for his perspicacity.
translations.idiomatic: Following her words, they captured the culprit; at the time he was praised for his perspicacity.

sentences.zh: 武平初，遷太師、司州牧。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was promoted to Grand Preceptor and Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuping he was promoted to Grand Preceptor and Governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州刺史，加太宰，遷右丞相、都督、青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Ji Province, given the additional title of Grand Steward, then transferred to Right Chancellor, Area Commander, and Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Ji Province, given the additional title of Grand Steward, then transferred to Right Chancellor, Area Commander, and Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 湝頻牧大蕃，雖不潔己，然寬恕，為吏人所懷。

translations.literal: Tang repeatedly governed great territories; though not personally incorruptible, he was lenient and won the attachment of officials and commoners alike.
translations.idiomatic: Tang repeatedly governed great territories; though not personally incorruptible, he was lenient and won the loyalty of officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 五年，青州人崔蔚波等夜襲州城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Cui Weibo of Qing Province and others attacked the provincial capital by night.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Cui Weibo of Qing Province and others attacked the provincial capital by night.

sentences.zh: 湝部分倉卒之際，咸得齊整，擊賊大破之。

translations.literal: Tang deployed his forces in the sudden emergency, each unit kept in good order, and struck the rebels a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Tang deployed his forces in the sudden emergency, every unit kept in good order, and struck the rebels a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 拜左丞相，轉瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Chancellor and transferred to Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Chancellor and transferred to Governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 及後主奔鄴，加湝大丞相。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord fled to Ye, Tang was given the additional title of Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord fled to Ye, Tang was given the additional title of Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及安德王稱尊號于晉陽，使劉子昂修啟於湝：「至尊出奔，宗廟既重，群公勸迫，權主號令。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ande proclaimed himself sovereign at Jinyang, he had Liu Ziang draft a missive to Tang: "The supreme sovereign has fled in exile; the ancestral temple weighs heavily upon us; the lords pressed their counsel, and we provisionally hold command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ande proclaimed himself sovereign at Jinyang, he had Liu Ziang draft a missive to Tang: "The supreme sovereign has fled in exile; the ancestral temple weighs heavily upon us; the lords pressed their counsel, and we provisionally hold command.

sentences.zh: 事甯終歸叔父。

translations.literal: When affairs are settled, power will ultimately return to you, Uncle.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs are settled, power will ultimately return to you, Uncle."

sentences.zh: 」湝曰：「我人臣，何容受此啟。

translations.literal: Tang said, "I am a subject—how could I accept such a missive?
translations.idiomatic: Tang said, "I am a subject—how could I accept such a missive?"

sentences.zh: 」執子昂送鄴。

translations.literal: He seized Liu Ziang and sent him to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Liu Ziang and sent him to Ye.

sentences.zh: 帝至濟州，禪位於湝，竟不達。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Ji Province he attempted to abdicate in Tang's favor, but the message never reached him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Ji Province he attempted to abdicate in Tang's favor, but the message never reached him.

sentences.zh: 湝與廣甯王孝珩于冀州召募，得四萬餘人，拒周軍。

translations.literal: Tang and Prince Xiaohang of Guangning raised troops in Ji Province, mustering more than forty thousand men to resist the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Prince Xiaohang of Guangning raised troops in Ji Province, mustering more than forty thousand men to resist the Zhou army.

sentences.zh: 周齊王憲來伐，先遣送書，並赦詔。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou came to attack, first sending ahead a letter along with an amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou came to attack, first sending ahead a letter along with an amnesty edict.

sentences.zh: 湝並沉諸井。

translations.literal: Tang had them all thrown into wells.
translations.idiomatic: Tang had them all thrown into wells.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，湝、孝珩俱被禽。

translations.literal: The battle lost, Tang and Xiaohang were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the battle was lost, Tang and Xiaohang were both taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「任城王，何苦至此！

translations.literal: Xian said, "Prince of Rencheng, why go to such lengths!"
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "Prince of Rencheng, why must you come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」湝曰：「下官神武帝子，兄弟十五人，幸而獨存。

translations.literal: Tang said, "Your humble servant is a son of Emperor Shenwu; of fifteen brothers, I alone by fortune survived."
translations.idiomatic: Tang said, "I am a son of Emperor Shenwu. Of fifteen brothers, I alone was spared."

sentences.zh: 逢宗社顛覆，今日得死，無愧墳陵。

translations.literal: Now that altars and state are overturned, to die today is to have no shame before the tombs."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the altars and state lie in ruin, to die today is to owe no shame to the ancestral graves."

sentences.zh: 」憲壯之，歸其妻子。

translations.literal: Xian admired him and returned his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was moved by his bearing and restored his wife and children to him.

sentences.zh: 將至鄴城，湝馬上大哭。

translations.literal: When they were about to reach Ye city, Tang wept aloud on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: As they neared Ye city, Tang broke into loud weeping on horseback.

sentences.zh: 自投於地，流血滿面。

translations.literal: He threw himself from the horse to the ground, blood covering his face.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself from the horse, blood streaming over his face.

sentences.zh: 至長安，尋與後主同死。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang'an, before long he died together with the Later Lord.
translations.idiomatic: After reaching Chang'an, he was soon put to death together with the Later Lord.

sentences.zh: 妃盧氏，賜斛斯徵。

translations.literal: His consort, the Lady Lu, was given to Husizheng.
translations.idiomatic: His consort, Lady Lu, was bestowed upon Husizheng.

sentences.zh: 盧蓬首垢面，長齋不言笑，徵放之，乃為尼。

translations.literal: Lu let her hair hang loose and her face go unwashed; she kept long fasts and neither spoke nor smiled. Husizheng released her, and she became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lu wore her hair loose and her face unwashed, kept long fasts, and neither spoke nor smiled. Husizheng released her, and she took the tonsure.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇三年，表請文帝，葬湝及五子于長安北原。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaihuang under Sui, a memorial was submitted to Emperor Wen to bury Tang and his five sons on the northern plain at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaihuang under Sui, a memorial was submitted to Emperor Wen requesting burial for Tang and his five sons on the northern plain at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高陽康穆王湜，神武第十一子也。

translations.literal: Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang, Shi, was the eleventh son of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang, Shi, was the eleventh son of Gao Huan, posthumously honored as Emperor Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 天保元年封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He received his enfeoffment in the first year of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 十年，稍遷尚書令。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was gradually promoted to Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was gradually promoted to Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以滑稽便辟，有寵于文宣。

translations.literal: Because he was witty and ingratiating, he won Wenxuan's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Witty and skilled at fawning, he won Wenxuan's favor.

sentences.zh: 在左右行杖，以撻諸王，太后深銜之。

translations.literal: Walking at the emperor's side with a staff, he used it to flog the other princes; the Empress Dowager deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: He walked at the emperor's side carrying a staff and used it to beat the other princes; the Empress Dowager deeply resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 其妃父護軍長史張晏之，嘗要道拜湜，湜不禮焉。

translations.literal: The father of his consort, Zhang Yanzhi, Chief Administrator of the Guard Corps, once blocked the road to pay his respects to Shi, but Shi did not return the courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanzhi, Chief Administrator of the Guard Corps and father of Shi's consort, once blocked the road to pay his respects, but Shi refused to acknowledge him.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，對曰：「無官職漢，何須禮！

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; he replied, "A Han man with no office—why should I show him courtesy!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked why, he replied, "A commoner with no office—why should I honor him?"

sentences.zh: 」帝於是擢拜晏之為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon promoted and appointed Yanzhi Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon promoted Yanzhi and appointed him Governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 文宣崩，湜兼司徒，導引梓官。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan died, Shi also served as Minister of Public Works and led the imperial coffin in procession.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan died, Shi also served as Minister of Public Works and led the imperial coffin in the funeral procession.

sentences.zh: 吹笛云：「至尊頗知臣不？

translations.literal: He played the flute and said, "Does His Majesty know me at all?"
translations.idiomatic: He played the flute and said, "Does His Majesty truly know me at all?"

sentences.zh: 」又擊胡鼓為樂。

translations.literal: He also beat a foreign drum for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He also beat a foreign drum for his own amusement.

sentences.zh: 太后杖湜百餘，未幾薨。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager beat Shi more than a hundred strokes; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager had Shi beaten more than a hundred times; before long he died.

sentences.zh: 太后哭之哀，曰：「我恐其不成就，與杖，何期帶創死也！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wept for him in deep grief and said, "I feared he would never amount to anything and gave him a beating—who expected he would die of wounds from it!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wept for him in anguish and said, "I feared he would never amount to anything and gave him a beating—who thought he would die of the wounds!"

sentences.zh: 」乾明初，贈假黃鉞、太師、司徒、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ganming he was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow axe, the posts of Grand Preceptor, Minister of Public Works, and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Ganming he was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow axe, Grand Preceptor, Minister of Public Works, and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子士義襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shiyi succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiyi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 博陵文簡王濟，神武第十二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Wenjian of Boling, Ji, was the twelfth son of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenjian of Boling, Ji, was the twelfth son of Gao Huan, posthumously honored as Emperor Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 天保元年封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He received his enfeoffment in the first year of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 濟嘗從文宣巡幸，在路忽憶太后，遂逃歸。

translations.literal: Ji once accompanied Wenxuan on a tour; on the road he suddenly thought of the Empress Dowager and fled back home.
translations.idiomatic: Ji once accompanied Wenxuan on tour; on the road he suddenly longed for the Empress Dowager and fled home.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，臨以白刃，因此驚怳。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and threatened him with bare blades; because of this he fell into shock and confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and threatened him with drawn blades; from this he fell into shock and confusion.

sentences.zh: 歷位太尉。

translations.literal: Through successive posts he rose to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 河清初，出為定州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Heqing he was sent out as Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Heqing he was sent out as Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 天統五年，在州語人云：「計次第，亦應到我。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiantong, while in the province he told people, "Counting in order of succession, it ought to reach me next."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tiantong, while governing the province he told others, "Counting in order of succession, my turn ought to come next."

sentences.zh: 」後主聞之，陰使人殺之。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord heard of it, he secretly sent men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord heard of this, he secretly sent men to kill him.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、太尉、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow axe, Grand Commandant, and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow axe, Grand Commandant, and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子智襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Zhi succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 馮翊王潤，字子澤，神武第十四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Fengyi Run, styled Zize, was the fourteenth son of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fengyi, Run, styled Zize, was the fourteenth son of Gao Huan, posthumously honored as Emperor Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 幼時，神武稱曰：「此吾家千里駒也。

translations.literal: In his youth Shenwu said of him, "This is the thousand-league colt of our house."
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Gao Huan said of him, "This is the thousand-league colt of our house."

sentences.zh: 」天保初封，歷位東北道行台右僕射、都督、定州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed, and through successive posts served as Right Vice Director of the Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Northeast Circuit, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed at the beginning of Tianbao and rose through successive posts to Right Vice Director of the Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Northeast Circuit, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 潤美姿儀。

translations.literal: Run was handsome in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Run was handsome in bearing.

sentences.zh: 年十四五，母鄭妃與之同寢，有穢雜之聲。

translations.literal: At fourteen or fifteen, his mother Princess Zheng slept in the same bed with him, and there were obscene sounds.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen or fifteen, his mother Princess Zheng shared his bed, and obscene sounds were heard.

sentences.zh: 及長，廉慎方雅，習於吏職。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was honest, cautious, upright, and elegant, and well practiced in official duties.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he was honest, cautious, upright, and refined, and well versed in administrative work.

sentences.zh: 至於摘發隱偽，奸吏無所匿其情。

translations.literal: When it came to exposing hidden wrongdoing, corrupt officials had nowhere to conceal their deeds.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to exposing hidden wrongdoing, corrupt officials could conceal nothing from him.

sentences.zh: 開府王回洛，與六州大都督獨孤枝侵竊官田，受納賄賂，潤按舉其事。

translations.literal: Wang Huailuo of the princely establishment and Dugu Zhi, Grand Commander of the Six Provinces, encroached on public fields and accepted bribes; Run investigated and impeached them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huailuo of the princely establishment and Dugu Zhi, Grand Commander of the Six Provinces, had encroached on public fields and taken bribes; Run investigated and impeached them.

sentences.zh: 二人表言：王出送台使，登魏孝文舊壇，南望歎息，不測其意。

translations.literal: The two men memorialized, saying the prince had gone out to escort an imperial envoy, climbed the old altar of Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, looked south, and sighed—his intent could not be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: The two men memorialized that the prince, while escorting an imperial envoy, had climbed the old altar of Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, looked south, and sighed—his intent could not be fathomed.

sentences.zh: 武成使元文遙就州宣敕曰：「馮翊王少小謹慎，在州不為非法，朕信之熟矣。

translations.literal: Wucheng sent Yuan Wenyao to the province to proclaim an edict, saying, "The Prince of Fengyi has been careful since youth; in the province he has done nothing unlawful—I trust him thoroughly."
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng sent Yuan Wenyao to the province to proclaim an edict: "The Prince of Fengyi has been careful since youth; in his province he has done nothing unlawful—I trust him completely."

sentences.zh: 登高遠望，人之常情，鼠輩欲輕相間構，曲生眉目。

translations.literal: To climb high and gaze into the distance is human nature; petty men wished lightly to sow discord between us and fabricated details out of nothing."
translations.idiomatic: To climb high and gaze into the distance is only human; petty men wished to drive a wedge between us and invented the whole affair."

sentences.zh: 」於是回洛決鞭二百，獨孤枝決杖一百。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huailuo was sentenced to two hundred strokes of the whip and Dugu Zhi to one hundred strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Huailuo was thereupon sentenced to two hundred strokes of the whip and Dugu Zhi to one hundred strokes of the staff.

sentences.zh: 尋為尚書令，領太子少師，曆司徒、太尉、大司馬、司州牧、太保、河南道行台、錄尚書，別封文成郡公，太師、太宰，復為定州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, and successively Minister of Public Works, Grand Commandant, Grand Marshal, Governor of Si Province, Grand Guardian, Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Henan Circuit, Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat; he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Wencheng Commandery, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Mentor, then again became Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, then successively Minister of Public Works, Grand Commandant, Grand Marshal, Governor of Si Province, Grand Guardian, head of the Henan Circuit Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat; he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Wencheng Commandery and promoted to Grand Preceptor and Grand Mentor, then again appointed Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈假黃鉞、左丞相。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow axe and Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow axe and Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 子茂德嗣。

translations.literal: His son Maode succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Maode succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 漢陽敬懷王洽，字敬延，神武第十五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang, Qia, styled Jingyan, was the fifteenth son of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang, Qia, styled Jingyan, was the fifteenth son of Gao Huan, posthumously honored as Emperor Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 天保元年封，五年薨，年十三。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed in the first year of Tianbao, he died in the fifth year, aged thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed in the first year of Tianbao, he died in the fifth year, aged thirteen.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年，贈太保、司空。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ganming he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ganming he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 無子，以任城王第二子建德為後。

translations.literal: Having no son, Jiande, the second son of the Prince of Rencheng, was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, Jiande, the second son of the Prince of Rencheng, was appointed his heir.

sentences.zh: 論曰：趙郡王以跗萼之親，當顧命之重，安夫一德，固此貞必，踐畏途而不疑，履危機而莫懼，以其忠義，取斃凶匿。

translations.literal: The historians comment: The Prince of Zhao Commandery, by virtue of the closest fraternal kinship, bore the weight of a dying sovereign's charge; he sought to secure the realm through unified loyalty, firm in integrity and resolution, treading a perilous path without hesitation and facing crisis without fear—and so, for his loyalty and righteousness, met death while treacherous men lurked in hiding.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: The Prince of Zhao Commandery, bound to the throne as calyx to flower, bore the weight of the dying sovereign's charge. He sought to hold the realm together through single-minded loyalty, steadfast in integrity, treading a perilous path without wavering and facing crisis without fear—and so, for his loyalty and righteousness, he met death while villains schemed in the shadows.

sentences.zh: 豈道光四海，不遇周成之明；

translations.literal: Was it that his virtue shone over the four seas, yet he did not meet a ruler with the clarity of King Cheng of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Was it that his virtue illumined the four seas, yet he found no ruler with the clarity of King Cheng of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 將朝去三仁，終見殷墟之禍。

translations.literal: or that the court drove away the Three Worthies and in the end beheld the calamity of the Yin ruins?
translations.idiomatic: or that the court cast out the Three Worthies and in the end beheld the ruin of the Yin dynasty?

sentences.zh: 不然，則邦國殄瘁，何若斯之速歟？

translations.literal: Otherwise, how could the altars and state have perished so swiftly?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how could the altars and state have collapsed so swiftly?

sentences.zh: 清河屬經綸之期，青雲自致，出將入相，翊成鴻業。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qinghe came of age in the time of founding and planning; he rose to the clouds by his own merit, going out as general and in as minister, and helped build the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qinghe came of age in the era of state-building; he rose by his own merit, going out as general and in as minister, and helped establish the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 雖漢朝劉賈，魏室曹洪，俱未足諭其風烈，適足以彰文宣之失德焉。

translations.literal: Even Liu Jia of Han and Cao Hong of Wei fall short of matching his stature and heroism; this only serves to reveal Wenxuan's lack of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Even Liu Jia of Han and Cao Hong of Wei cannot fully measure up to his stature and heroism—and that fact alone exposes Wenxuan's want of virtue.

sentences.zh: 思好屬昏亂之機，歸彥因猜嫌之釁，咫尺鄴都，以速其禍，智小謀大，理則宜然。

translations.literal: Sihao seized the moment of chaos; Guiyan exploited mutual suspicion—both within a stone's throw of Ye city, yet both hastened to disaster. Small wisdom, grand designs: by reason it could not have been otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: Sihao seized the hour of chaos; Guiyan exploited mutual suspicion—both within a stone's throw of Ye, yet both hastened to ruin. Small wisdom paired with grand ambition: by right it could not have ended otherwise.

sentences.zh: 神武諸王，多有聲譽。

translations.literal: Among the sons of Shenwu, many enjoyed fine reputations.
translations.idiomatic: Of Shenwu's sons, many enjoyed fine reputations.

sentences.zh: 永安以諫爭遇禍，固齊室之比干，彭城蒞人布政，乃與循良比跡，求之近古，未為易遇。

translations.literal: Prince Yong'an met calamity through remonstrance—truly the Bigan of the Qi house; Prince Pengcheng governed the people and spread good policy, ranking with the finest administrators—sought in recent antiquity, such men were not easily found.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong'an met disaster through remonstrance—truly the Bigan of the Qi house; Prince Pengcheng governed the people and spread good policy, ranking with the finest administrators—such men were not easily found even in recent antiquity.

sentences.zh: 上党申威淮海，受辱牢阱，以英俠之氣，迫悲歌之思，欲食藜藿之羹，處茅茨之下，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Prince Shangdang displayed his might on the Huai-Hai frontier, yet suffered disgrace in an iron cage; with the spirit of a hero forced toward mournful song, could he still eat coarse vegetable broth and dwell beneath a thatched roof?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shangdang displayed his might on the Huai-Hai frontier, yet suffered disgrace in a dungeon; with a hero's spirit pressed toward lament, could he still eat coarse vegetable broth and live beneath a thatched roof?

sentences.zh: 馮翊廉慎閑明，妄被讒匿，以武成陰忌之朝，而見免夫《角弓》之刺，已為幸矣。

translations.literal: Prince Fengyi was honest, cautious, and clear-minded, yet was falsely slandered; in Wucheng's secretly jealous court, to be spared the sting of the Jiaogong complaint was already fortune enough.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fengyi was honest, cautious, and clear-minded, yet was falsely slandered; in Wucheng's secretly jealous court, to escape the sting of the Jiaogong complaint was already a mercy.
